question: Emergency vehicles using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights:
options: a:Have the right-of-way and drivers must yield to them.,b:May follow each other and you should proceed only when sure the way is clear.,c:May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
note: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens or lights; obey instructions and ensure the path is clear before proceeding.

question: What shape/color represents the slow-moving vehicle emblem?
options: a:Reflective orange triangle (commonly shown on a yellow/orange background),b:Rectangular red sign,c:Circular green sign,d:Diamond-shaped yellow sign
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange (sometimes bordered) triangle indicating a vehicle likely traveling 25 mph or less.

question: Which are ways alcoholic beverages can affect you?
options: a:They slow reaction time, impair thinking, and give a false sense of confidence.,b:They always improve alertness.,c:They only cause sleepiness but not coordination problems.,d:They only affect people who are under 21.
note: Alcohol slows reaction time, impairs judgment and thinking, and can produce false confidence and poor coordination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.,b:All crossings have flashing signals and gates.,c:You never need to stop if no train is visible.
note: Driving around lowered gates is unlawful. Not all crossings have gates or signals; always obey signs, flags, and warning devices.

question: If you are involved in an accident as a driver, you should:
options: a:Exchange information such as names, addresses, license and insurance details.,b:Refuse to share any details.,c:Leave immediately and call later.,d:Only give your name without other details.
note: Exchange full information with other drivers, including names, addresses, license numbers, vehicle data, and insurance details.

question: Turn signal lights on vehicles manufactured after 1955 must be visible for at least how many feet?
options: a:250 feet,b:300 feet,c:500 feet
note: Required front and rear turn signal lamps must be visible for at least 300 feet in normal daylight conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the centerline shows a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, when may you pass?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:If you are on an expressway.,c:If traffic is clear
note: When the broken line is next to your lane, you may cross to pass if no oncoming traffic is present and it is safe to do so.

question: A single broken white line between lanes indicates what?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers may change lanes when safe.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers may pass when safe.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed when it is safe to change lanes.

question: What must you do when you encounter a flashing red traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, then proceed when the way is clear.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping,c:Wait until a green light appears,d:Yield only to pedestrians
note: A flashing red light is equivalent to a stop sign: stop fully, then go when safe.

question: When weather changes suddenly, what should you do?
options: a:Be particularly aware of vehicles coming up behind you in inclement weather.,b:A sudden change in weather calls for a change in driving.,c:You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
note: If the weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving to match conditions — slow down in rain or fog and be aware of vehicles behind you that may not be slowing.

question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Stop and do not turn in the direction of the arrow until it changes.,b:The arrow is decorative only and may be ignored,c:Proceed with caution and yield to pedestrians,d:You may turn after yielding to oncoming traffic
note: A solid red arrow indicates traffic in that lane must stop and may not turn in the arrow's direction until it changes.

question: If a police officer stops your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.,b:Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach you.,c:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
note: Remain in your vehicle with hands visible on the wheel and wait for the officer’s instructions; only retrieve documents when asked.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, how should you position your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,b:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,c:Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.,d:Leave the wheels in neutral
note: When parked facing uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb so if brakes fail the vehicle rolls into the curb rather than into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck and no gates or flashing lights, how should you proceed?
options: a:Approach with extreme caution and only cross when you are sure no train is coming.,b:Turn down the radio to try to hear a train.,c:Only proceed if a flagger clears you to go.
note: Always approach crossings cautiously and do not cross until you have determined no train is coming; obey any flagger if present.

question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is most likely:
options: a:Blind or visually impaired.,b:Deaf.,c:Part of a traffic study.,d:Directing traffic.
note: Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian who is using a white cane or guide dog.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should your vehicle end up?
options: a:In the left lane of the one-way street,b:In the center of the roadway,c:In the right lane of the one-way street,d:Across two lanes
note: When turning left onto a one-way street from a two-way street, complete the turn into the leftmost lane available on the one-way street.

question: Which is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Bad weather,b:Human error,c:New drivers
note: Most crashes are caused by human error — mistakes like failing to see other vehicles, misjudging distance, or making poor decisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should always signal when:
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.,d:All of the above
note: Use turn signals to indicate your intentions whenever changing lanes, entering traffic, or parking so other road users can respond.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A shared center lane on a two-way road is reserved for:
options: a:Making left turns.,b:Passing slow-moving traffic.,c:Through traffic.
note: Shared center lanes are for left turns (and U-turns where permitted), not for passing or through traffic.

question: If other drivers are acting angrily, what should you do?
options: a:React with hand gestures.,b:Distance yourself from the situation and avoid eye contact.,c:Make eye contact to defuse the situation.
note: Mentally and physically distance yourself: avoid eye contact or gestures, slow down or change lanes, and remove yourself safely from the situation.

question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed when driving in the rain.,b:Ensure that your tires are properly inflated.,c:Ensure that your tires have good tread depth.,d:All of the above
note: Prevent hydroplaning by keeping tires in good condition and reducing speed in wet conditions; hydroplaning is most likely at higher speeds.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim high beams, you should look toward which part of the road?
options: a:The right side of the road.,b:The center of the road.,c:Either side equally.,d:The left shoulder.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the roadway to avoid being blinded by high beams while maintaining your lane position.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what is the best response?
options: a:Flash your lights to let them know they're wrong.,b:Call the police immediately.,c:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
note: Avoid escalation by staying calm and getting out of the aggressive driver's path; do not engage or retaliate.

question: A yellow and black diamond-shaped sign serves to:
options: a:Warn you about conditions on or near the road.,b:Help direct you to cities and towns ahead.,c:Inform you about traffic laws and regulations.
note: Diamond-shaped yellow-and-black signs are warning signs that advise of conditions or hazards ahead on the roadway.

question: Which will help someone overcome the influence of alcohol?
options: a:Fresh air,b:Hot coffee,c:Tomato juice and lime,d:Only the passage of time
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize alcohol; coffee, fresh air, or other remedies do not reduce intoxication.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:The speed your vehicle is traveling.,b:The condition of your brakes and tires.,c:The condition of the pavement.,d:All of the above
note: Braking distance is influenced by speed, vehicle maintenance (brakes and tires), and road surface conditions.

question: If you see an animal on the road, what is the correct action?
options: a:Pass the animal as closely as possible.,b:No special action is required.,c:Proceed cautiously and pass slowly to avoid startling it.
note: Slow down and pass animals carefully to avoid frightening them and causing unpredictable movement that could cause a crash.

question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and diagonal slash most commonly indicates:
options: a:That drivers should come to a complete stop.,b:That an action is forbidden.,c:That some drivers should yield to others.
note: A red circle with a slash over a black symbol indicates the action shown is prohibited by law.

question: If you are in the left lane and want to move into the right lane, you should:
options: a:Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for vehicles before changing lanes.,b:Look over your left shoulder only.,c:Signal and immediately move right without checking mirrors.,d:Honk and move over quickly.
note: When changing lanes to the right, check mirrors, signal, and glance over your right shoulder to confirm the blind spot is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an intersection with a steady green light, you should:
options: a:Continue driving, unless there are vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.,c:Stop if a police officer is nearby.
note: You may go on green but must yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection and be prepared to stop if conditions change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different highways at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,b:Either one may proceed at will,c:The vehicle on the right must yield,d:The faster vehicle goes first
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: Why must you be cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:The bicyclist may swerve unexpectedly or obstacles may force them into traffic.,b:Bicycles always have the right-of-way in every situation.,c:Oncoming traffic cannot see you if you pass a bicycle,d:Bicyclists are required to hug the curb at all times
note: Cyclists may need to swerve to avoid debris or hazards; give them space and pass carefully.

question: If borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Disregard obvious defects to avoid embarrassment.,b:Assume all vehicles work the same and just start driving.,c:Familiarize yourself with the controls and check for defects before driving.
note: Before driving an unfamiliar car, locate and test signals, lights, wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn; correct any defects first.

question: What's the key rule about managing speed when negotiating curves?
options: a:Brake hard in the middle of the curve,b:Slow down before entering the curve, not while at the sharpest point.,c:Maintain posted speed through the entire curve regardless,d:Accelerate before you enter a curve to maintain momentum
note: You should reduce speed before entering a curve, not while you are at the sharpest part. Braking hard in the middle of a curve can cause skidding or loss of control. Enter at a safe speed, then maintain a steady speed and accelerate gently as you exit if conditions allow.

question: If you’re in an accident and your vehicle is blocking traffic, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Move the vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway.,b:Remain where you are until police arrive.,c:Immediately leave the scene to get help.,d:Abandon the vehicle and flag down traffic
note: After a minor crash, if no one is seriously injured and the vehicles are drivable, you should move them out of the traffic lane to the shoulder or a safe area. This helps prevent additional collisions. You must stay at the scene, exchange information, and render aid as required by law.

question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, you should:
options: a:Pull next to the driver and yell at them.,b:Let it go.,c:Flash your high beams at the driver.
note: If another driver cuts you off, the safest response is to stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and continue driving defensively. Reacting aggressively can quickly escalate into road rage and greatly increase the risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A Reduced speed, 35 mph sign means:
options: a:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at the next speed limit sign.,b:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at this sign.,c:That you have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
note: A reduced speed sign means the new posted speed limit applies starting at the sign itself. You must have already slowed to that speed by the time you reach the sign, not sometime later.

question: While driving on major highways, what habits help you stay safe?
options: a:Keep your eyes moving, stay alert, and be ready to react to hazards.,b:Look at one point on the road to reduce distractions.,c:Use cruise control at all times.
note: On highways, you reduce risk by constantly scanning with your eyes, checking mirrors, and staying alert so you can react early to hazards. Staring at one point can cause highway hypnosis, and cruise control should only be used when conditions are safe and appropriate.

question: You should honk your horn when you:
options: a:Are traveling through an intersection.,b:Are passing a bicyclist.,c:See a child who is about to run into the street.
note: Use your horn to warn others of immediate danger, such as a child about to run into the street. Avoid using the horn unnecessarily, since that can startle other road users and create new hazards.

question: What is a good rule to follow when considering passing another vehicle?
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when necessary and legal.,b:Pass on the right whenever possible regardless of conditions.,c:Try to get ahead by passing multiple cars frequently,d:Always pass trucks since they obstruct vision
note: Passing always carries extra risk. It is safest to travel with the flow of traffic and pass only when it is clearly legal, necessary, and you have enough space and visibility to complete the maneuver safely.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.,c:Passing on the left is permitted from either direction
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. Vehicles on the side with the broken line may cross it to pass when it is safe. Vehicles on the side with the solid line must not cross the line to pass.

question: When approaching an accident scene, you should:
options: a:Keep moving and do not slow down to look at the accident.,b:Keep your attention on your driving and watch for people or vehicles near the road.,c:Stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived.
note: When approaching an accident scene, you should not stop or slow down unnecessarily just to look, because this creates additional hazards and congestion. Only stop if you are directly involved in the crash or if emergency help has not yet arrived and your assistance is needed. Otherwise, keep moving carefully, stay alert, and watch for people or vehicles in or near the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing on a multilane highway, you must:
options: a:Signal and ensure the passing lane is clear.,b:Pass only on the right under all circumstances.,c:Assume oncoming traffic will stop.,d:Sound your horn before changing lanes.
note: Before passing on a multilane highway, you must check that the lane you will move into is clear of traffic, check your mirrors and blind spot, and signal before changing lanes. Never assume other drivers will slow or stop for you; it is your responsibility to make sure the maneuver can be done safely.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Use your parking lights.,b:Use your low beams.,c:Use your high beams.
note: In fog, use low-beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and create glare, making it harder to see. Parking lights alone do not provide enough light or make you visible enough to others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A two-lane road divided by a broken yellow centerline indicates:
options: a:No passing is allowed in either direction.,b:Traffic moves in the same direction.,c:This road is under repair.,d:Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
note: A broken yellow centerline on a two-lane road means traffic travels in opposite directions and passing is allowed in either direction when it is safe. You may cross the broken yellow line to pass, but only when you have enough clear distance and no oncoming traffic or other hazards.

question: You have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the signal. What should you do?
options: a:Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.,b:Speed up and pass in front of them.,c:Honk your horn to warn them.
note: Even if you have a green light, you must yield to pedestrians already in the crosswalk, even when they are crossing against the signal. Slow or stop as needed to avoid hitting them and wait until they are safely out of your path before proceeding.

question: If another driver behaves aggressively toward you, how should you respond?
options: a:Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.,b:Retaliate by tailgating them.,c:Cut them off to slow them down.
note: When another driver is aggressive, your goal is to avoid conflict and reduce risk. Do not make eye contact or respond with gestures, and do not speed up or race. Instead, slow down slightly, create space, and let the aggressive driver pass when it is safe.

question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It has no effect in small amounts.,b:It improves driving skills.,c:It affects only judgment but not motor skills.,d:It harms both driving skills and judgment.
note: Alcohol begins to affect the brain and body with the first drink. It slows reaction time, reduces coordination, affects vision, and weakens judgment and decision‑making. Because it harms both your physical driving skills and your judgment, any amount can make driving unsafe.

question: Approaching a flashing red traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Treat it like a stop sign: stop, yield, then proceed when safe.,b:Continue through if there is no cross traffic.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection.,d:Ignore it and follow the flow of traffic.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the limit line or before the crosswalk, look for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield to anyone with the right‑of‑way, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: Where on the roadway are icy patches likely to form first and last to dry?
options: a:Sections in the sun.,b:Sections shaded by trees or buildings.,c:Curvy sections of the road.
note: In cold or freezing conditions, areas that stay shaded—such as spots under trees, bridges, or next to buildings—freeze before sunny areas and stay icy longer. Be especially cautious and reduce speed on these shaded sections, even if the rest of the road looks clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Make a quick U-turn across the median,b:Cut across traffic to reach the exit,c:Back up on the shoulder to reach the exit,d:Continue to the next exit and do not stop or turn around on the roadway.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, you must continue to the next exit. Never stop in a travel lane, back up on the shoulder, cut across traffic, or make a U‑turn across the median. Those maneuvers are illegal and extremely dangerous at freeway speeds.

question: Orange-colored traffic signs are typically used to indicate what?
options: a:Regulatory instructions such as speed limits.,b:School zones,c:Work zones and construction areas.,d:Recreational areas
note: Orange signs are temporary warning signs used for work zones and construction areas. They alert you to road work, lane shifts, workers, and equipment so you can slow down, be prepared to stop, and follow any special directions.

question: On slippery roads, how should you adjust your driving speed relative to the posted limit?
options: a:Maintain the posted speed at all times,b:Slow down and drive more slowly than the posted speed if conditions require.,c:Speed up slightly to maintain control,d:Use cruise control to stabilize speed
note: On slippery roads, you must slow down below the posted speed limit as needed for conditions. The speed limit is the maximum in ideal conditions; when it’s wet, icy, or snowy, safe driving often requires going significantly slower and making smooth, gentle steering and braking inputs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should not pass another vehicle:
options: a:On a hill or curve.,b:When approaching an intersection.,c:When a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended.
note: You must never pass when a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended; traffic in most or all directions must stop until the lights stop flashing. Passing on hills, curves, or near intersections is also often prohibited because your view or space is limited, but the most critical rule is to always stop for a school bus with flashing red lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may proceed carefully through an intersection with a yellow light if:
options: a:When you cannot stop safely before the intersection and are already too close to the stop line.,b:When you are already within the intersection.,c:Both a and b.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If the light turns yellow after you have already entered the intersection and you cannot stop safely, you should continue through carefully. You should not enter the intersection on yellow if you can stop safely before the stop line.

question: When rain begins while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.,b:Drive faster than surrounding traffic.,c:Slow down.
note: When rain first begins, oil and dirt on the road mix with the water and make the surface very slippery. You should slow down, turn on your headlights so others can see you, and increase your following distance. If visibility becomes too poor, pull over safely and wait for conditions to improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down until it passes you.,b:Drive with your flashers on and slow down.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: When you hear or see an emergency vehicle using a siren and flashing lights, you must yield the right‑of‑way. Safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed. Do not keep driving alongside it or in front of it, and do not use your flashers to move with it.

question: Which effect does alcohol have on driving performance?
options: a:Slows reflexes and reaction time.,b:Wakes you up.,c:Puts you to sleep.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain and nervous system activity. It reduces your reflexes, lengthens your reaction time, and harms your judgment and coordination, all of which make safe driving much more difficult and increase crash risk.

question: What can happen when you consume alcohol while taking other drugs?
options: a:It will decrease the effects of the drugs and alcohol.,b:It can increase the effects of both the drugs and alcohol.,c:It helps cure certain illnesses
note: Mixing alcohol with other drugs, including many prescription or over‑the‑counter medicines, can greatly increase the effects of both. This can cause extreme drowsiness, poor coordination, and dangerously impaired judgment, making it unsafe and illegal to drive.

question: When near a blind pedestrian using a cane or guide dog, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed normally if you have the right-of-way.,b:Take the right-of-way to keep traffic flowing.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: Blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog have the right‑of‑way. You must slow down, be prepared to stop, and allow them plenty of time and space to cross safely. Never honk, rush them, or try to direct them; let them determine when it is safe to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required but there is no marked line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:At the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic without entering it.,b:You are not required to stop,c:Only at a place where you can see 200 feet both ways by entering the roadway,d:At least 20 feet before the intersection
note: When there is a stop requirement but no stop line or crosswalk, you must stop before entering the intersection at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can clearly see approaching traffic. This keeps you out of the intersection while still allowing you to check for cross traffic and pedestrians.

question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you do?
options: a:Back up on the shoulder to reach the exit.,b:Make a quick lane change to the exit lane.,c:Continue to the next exit or safe place to turn around
note: If you miss your freeway exit, stay calm, keep going, and continue to the next exit or another safe, legal place to turn around. Never stop, back up, or make sudden lane changes on a freeway, as these actions can cause serious crashes.

question: To reduce headlight glare from oncoming drivers, where should you look?
options: a:Straight ahead at the center of the road.,b:At the right side of the road ahead.,c:Over your shoulder.
note: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the white line or road edge as a guide. This helps protect your night vision while still letting you monitor your lane position and the road ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when you meet an oncoming vehicle, what must you allow?
options: a:At least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the roadway to the oncoming vehicle.,b:For the other vehicle to pull over completely every time.,c:To demand the other vehicle back up,d:To pass on the shoulder
note: On narrow two-way roads, each driver must yield at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the roadway to oncoming traffic. Sharing the roadway this way allows both vehicles to pass safely without forcing either driver off the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, what is the general recommended action?
options: a:Accelerate on the ramp to match the speed of traffic and merge when safe.,b:Enter slowly to avoid disturbing other drivers,c:Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a large gap,d:Always enter above the speed limit
note: When entering a highway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to build up speed so it closely matches the flow of traffic. Signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge into a suitable gap without stopping, unless traffic or signs require you to stop.

question: A single dashed yellow centerline between lanes means:
options: a:The road is one-way.,b:Drivers may not pass in either direction.,c:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,d:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
note: A single dashed yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line is dashed (broken), drivers in both directions may cross it to pass another vehicle, but only when it is safe and legal to do so and when there is no oncoming traffic close enough to create a hazard.

question: A pedestrian begins crossing in front of your vehicle. What should you do?
options: a:Stop and wait until the pedestrian has finished crossing.,b:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,d:Flash your headlights to warn the pedestrian.
note: Slow down and be prepared to stop whenever you see pedestrians walking or crossing the roadway; always yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk.

question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:
options: a:Assume the guard is not supposed to be directing traffic.,b:Copy what surrounding traffic is doing, despite the crossing guard's instructions.,c:Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.,d:Proceed only if the traffic signal is green, ignoring the crossing guard.
note: Crossing guards have legal authority to control traffic in school zones. You must obey their signals and instructions just as you would obey a traffic signal or police officer. Slow down, be prepared to stop, and follow the guard’s directions to protect children and other pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the proper lane, you should:
options: a:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the correct lane.,b:Quickly cut across lanes to make the turn.,c:Signal and make the turn from your current lane.,d:Stop in the intersection and wait for a gap.
note: If you are not in the correct lane to make a turn when you reach an intersection, continue straight and go to the next intersection where you can get into the proper lane. Sudden lane changes or turning from the wrong lane can surprise other drivers and cause crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at a four-way stop simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left.,b:The driver who honks first.,c:The driver on the right.,d:The driver going straight.
note: At a four‑way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The driver on the right has the right‑of‑way and may proceed first when it is safe. Never use your horn to claim the right‑of‑way.

question: Defensive driving is best described as:
options: a:Following the vehicle ahead very closely.,b:Driving only during daylight hours.,c:Racing to get ahead of aggressive drivers.,d:Identifying dangerous situations early and taking action to avoid collisions.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road, spotting potential hazards early, and adjusting your speed or position to avoid trouble. Instead of reacting at the last second, you leave space, anticipate other drivers’ mistakes, and make calm, safe choices to prevent collisions.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear its siren, you must:
options: a:Keep driving in your lane.,b:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.,c:Pull to the right curb and stop.
note: Immediately pull to the curb or side of the road and stop, allowing the emergency vehicle to pass safely.

question: When passing a large vehicle, a small vehicle driver should be prepared for:
options: a:Excessive fuel consumption.,b:Reduced visibility of road signs only.,c:Wind gusts from the larger vehicle that may affect steering.,d:Loud music only.
note: Large trucks and buses push a lot of air around them, creating wind gusts and turbulence. When you pass or are passed by a large vehicle, your car can be pushed or pulled sideways, so keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, avoid lingering in blind spots, and be ready to make small steering corrections.

question: If you are worried, nervous, angry, or crying, you should:
options: a:Drive no differently than you would if you were thinking more clearly.,b:Take the time to focus on driving before starting the engine.,c:Drive faster because you are more in touch with your senses.
note: Strong emotions like anger, fear, or sadness can distract you, slow your reactions, and lead to risky decisions. Before driving, take time to calm down and focus so your full attention is on the road, your speed, and surrounding traffic.

question: Which factors can impair a person's ability to drive safely?
options: a:A lack of sleep.,b:Any medication.,c:Alcohol.,d:All of the above.
note: Driving can be impaired by alcohol, many medications (including some that are legal and prescribed), and a lack of sleep. All of these can slow your reaction time, affect judgment, and reduce awareness, making it unsafe to drive.

question: What is the first control you should adjust when you get into a car to drive?
options: a:Adjust the rearview mirror only after driving,b:Adjust your seat so you can reach controls and see clearly.,c:Adjust the steering wheel first,d:Fasten your seatbelt after you begin driving
note: Before driving, adjust your seat first so you can comfortably reach the pedals, steering wheel, and other controls and have a clear view of the road. Once your seating position is correct, you then adjust mirrors and other controls so they are properly aligned to your driving position.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended, drivers should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.,b:Honk their horn before passing the bus on its left.,c:Continue driving when they think most kids are probably done exiting the bus.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, unless you are in one of the limited, clearly defined exceptions in your state (such as on the opposite side of a divided highway). This protects children who may be crossing the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection is blocked ahead by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Do not enter the intersection; wait until you can pass completely through.,b:Edge forward until you can see better,c:Enter the intersection and stop in the middle,d:Honk to signal other drivers to move
note: You should not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it without stopping. Entering when traffic is backed up can leave your vehicle blocking the intersection, which is unsafe, causes gridlock, and is illegal in many jurisdictions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles reach a four-way stop simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle on the left goes first,b:Both must wait for a signal,c:The larger vehicle proceeds first,d:The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way; the vehicle on the left yields.
note: At a four‑way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps decide who goes first when there is no traffic signal and both drivers arrive together.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following statements about passing is true?
options: a:Never look over your shoulder when passing.,b:Only signal after you start to pass.,c:You may return to your lane as soon as the other vehicle's bumper is aligned with your front.,d:Signal at least 100 feet ahead, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot when passing to the left.
note: When passing to the left, you should signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Only move back into your original lane when you are safely ahead of the vehicle you passed, typically when you can see that vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.

question: If you hit an unattended parked car and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Leave a written notice with your name, address, and accident details.,b:Drive away after inspecting both vehicles,c:Only call your insurance and leave without notifying anyone,d:Wait until someone else finds the owner
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot locate the owner, you must stop and leave a written note in a secure, visible place on the vehicle with your name, address, and a brief description of what happened. You must also report the collision to law enforcement if required by your state’s damage or injury reporting thresholds.

question: Which best describes hydroplaning?
options: a:Your tires pushing water out of their paths.,b:Your tires gliding on a film of water.,c:Your tires causing sheets of water to splash on passing vehicles.
note: Hydroplaning occurs when your tires lose contact with the road and ride up on a thin film of water. When this happens, you can lose steering and braking control. Slowing down on wet roads and having properly inflated tires with good tread helps prevent hydroplaning.

question: What does the term 'No zone' refer to?
options: a:A one-way traffic area,b:The blind spot of a large vehicle,c:A designated no passing zone
note: The “No-Zone” is the large blind-spot area around trucks and other large vehicles where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. If you drive in these areas, the truck driver may not know you are there, increasing the risk of a collision. Avoid lingering alongside or close behind large vehicles.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:It improves engine performance.,b:It can allow carbon monoxide into the passenger compartment, causing poisoning.,c:It always leads to a blown tire.,d:It causes decreased fuel economy.
note: A leaky exhaust system can let carbon monoxide, a colorless and odorless poisonous gas, enter the passenger compartment. Breathing carbon monoxide can cause headache, dizziness, unconsciousness, and even death. Any suspected exhaust leak should be repaired immediately.

question: When are you permitted to cross solid yellow centerlines?
options: a:To make a turn into a driveway or side road.,b:At any time.,c:Only during daylight hours
note: Solid yellow centerlines generally mean no passing, but you may cross them when making a safe, lawful left turn into or out of a driveway, alley, or side road. You may not cross solid yellow lines just to pass another vehicle.

question: When driving in bad weather, how should you adjust your following distance?
options: a:Decrease your following distance.,b:Keep the same following distance as normal.,c:Increase your following distance
note: In rain, snow, fog, or other poor conditions, your stopping distance increases and it is harder to see hazards. You should leave more space between your vehicle and the one ahead so you have extra time to react and stop smoothly.

question: To avoid sudden braking or turning, how far ahead should you generally look down the road?
options: a:About 10 seconds ahead,b:Two seconds ahead,c:Four seconds ahead,d:One second ahead
note: Good defensive driving means scanning well ahead so you can see problems early. Most manuals recommend looking about 10–15 seconds ahead so you can change speed or lanes gradually instead of braking or turning suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:Speeding is safe if you are an experienced driver.,c:Speeding has no effect on crash severity
note: Driving much slower than surrounding traffic can cause sudden lane changes and rear-end collisions. You must adjust your speed to traffic and conditions, staying within the speed limit. Speeding always increases crash risk and crash severity.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before making a turn?
options: a:Activate your turn signal.,b:Turn the wheel before signaling.,c:Increase your speed
note: Before turning, you should signal early—usually at least 100 feet or about three to four seconds before the turn—so others know what you plan to do. Then slow as needed and turn only when it is safe.

question: How must traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings be treated?
options: a:They must always be obeyed.,b:They are only suggestions,c:They apply only when other traffic is present,d:They are optional on weekdays
note: Signs, signals, and pavement markings are legal controls that tell you when to stop, go, yield, change speed, or stay out of certain areas. You are required to obey them at all times unless directed otherwise by a police officer or traffic control person.

question: If a transit vehicle is signaling to re-enter the main roadway after stopping, you must:
options: a:Honk to let them know you’re there.,b:Move to the left lane.,c:Yield.
note: When a bus or other transit vehicle signals that it is leaving a stop and re-entering traffic, you should yield. Either slow down or change lanes if it is safe so the vehicle can merge smoothly. This reduces sudden braking and helps protect passengers who may still be near the vehicle.

question: Distracted driving can be caused by:
options: a:Changing a radio station or CD.,b:Eating, drinking, or smoking.,c:Talking or texting on a cellular phone.,d:All of the above
note: Any activity that takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving is a distraction. Adjusting the radio, eating or drinking, and using a phone all reduce your ability to react quickly and safely, increasing the chance of a crash.

question: Where is it particularly important to reduce your speed?
options: a:When the road is wet or slippery, on narrow or winding roads, near intersections and railroad crossings, on hills, and in curves.,b:Only on expressways.,c:Only on interstates.
note: You should reduce speed whenever conditions reduce traction or visibility, such as on wet or slippery roads, narrow or winding roads, near intersections and railroad crossings, on hills, and in curves. Slower speeds give you more time and distance to react and stop safely.

question: Why is night driving more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:Visibility is reduced in the dark.,b:Cars overheat more quickly at night.,c:It is more likely to rain at night.
note: At night you cannot see as far ahead, and your side vision is reduced. Because visibility is limited, hazards may appear suddenly and you have less time and distance to react. Use proper headlights, keep your speed reasonable for what you can see, and increase following distance.

question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
options: a:Whoever started moving last,b:The driver,c:Whoever is slower
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians who are lawfully crossing the street, including when the driver is turning and there is no traffic light. Yielding means slowing or stopping so the pedestrian can cross safely before you complete your turn.

question: To avoid collisions related to blind spots, you should:
options: a:Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.,b:Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.,c:Quickly turn your head to see if your blind spot is clear before changing lanes.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see with your mirrors alone. Before changing lanes or turning, you should quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to make sure the blind spot is clear. Do not rely only on mirrors or your horn to detect vehicles in these areas.

question: A flashing red traffic signal requires the same action as which sign?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A slow sign.,c:A yield sign.,d:A no-turn sign.
note: A flashing red traffic signal means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to pedestrians and other traffic, then proceed when it is safe.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:
options: a:Slow down.,b:Be ready to stop.,c:Look for a train.
note: When you approach a railroad crossing, you should slow down, look and listen for trains in both directions, and be prepared to stop. If warning lights are flashing, gates are lowered, or a train is clearly approaching, you must stop and wait until it is safe and the signals indicate you may proceed.

question: Is it legal to drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway?
options: a:If you aren't driving.,b:If you are riding in the back seat.,c:No — consuming alcohol in a vehicle on a public road is generally prohibited by open container laws.
note: It is illegal to consume or possess an open alcoholic beverage on public roads; open container laws prohibit having open alcohol where driver or passengers sit.

question: When must you stop for a school bus with flashing red lights on a two-lane highway?
options: a:Only if you are following the bus,b:Only if the bus is facing you,c:If the bus is stopped on the shoulder with no children present,d:You must stop in both directions until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted.
note: On a two-lane road with no median or physical divider, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended. Remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted, because children may be crossing the road from any direction.

question: On long trips, to prevent drowsiness you should:
options: a:Slow down slightly if needed, but understand speed alone does not prevent fatigue.,b:Keep the radio loud to stay awake.,c:Drive with one window open at all times.,d:Stop at regular intervals to rest, walk, and stretch.
note: On long trips, the safest way to prevent drowsiness is to stop at regular intervals to rest, walk, and stretch. Short breaks every couple of hours help you stay alert much more effectively than tricks like loud music or open windows, which do not reliably prevent fatigue.

question: What is the primary reason alcohol makes driving dangerous?
options: a:It improves coordination temporarily,b:It only affects peripheral vision.,c:It prevents drowsiness,d:It impairs judgment and driving skill.
note: Alcohol makes driving dangerous because it affects the brain areas that control judgment, decision‑making, and coordination. Even small amounts can slow your reactions, reduce your ability to judge speed and distance, and make it harder to steer and brake smoothly, greatly increasing crash risk.

question: What happens to your tires' effectiveness as you drive faster on wet roads?
options: a:They become less effective at clearing water and you risk hydroplaning.,b:Water does not affect cars with good tires.,c:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.,d:They become more effective at clearing water as speed increases.
note: As speed increases on wet roads, your tires have less time to squeeze water out from under the tread. This reduces traction and can cause hydroplaning, where the tires ride on top of the water and lose contact with the road. Slowing down in wet conditions is essential to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver who travels much slower than the flow of traffic:
options: a:Can be hazardous and may be required to pull off to let traffic pass.,b:Is always the safest driver.,c:Automatically has the right-of-way.,d:Should never allow others to pass.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be just as dangerous as speeding because it causes sudden braking, lane changes, and congestion. On many two‑lane roads, if several vehicles are lined up behind you, you are required to pull over safely and let them pass.

question: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian:
options: a:Only when the pedestrian is in a marked or unmarked crosswalk.,b:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.,c:Even if the pedestrian crosses the street carelessly.,d:Only when traffic signals give the pedestrian the right‑of‑way.
note: Drivers must use due care to avoid hitting pedestrians, even when pedestrians are crossing carelessly or outside a crosswalk. You must slow down or stop if necessary to avoid a collision, because a pedestrian is far more vulnerable than someone inside a vehicle.

question: How can stress affect your driving ability?
options: a:It can reduce your ability to concentrate and focus on driving.,b:It lowers your chance of having an accident.,c:Makes you immune to fatigue,d:Prevents you from committing traffic violations
note: Stress and strong emotions can distract you from the driving task, slow your reactions, and lead to poor decisions. When you are angry, upset, or under heavy stress, you are more likely to miss hazards, follow too closely, or drive aggressively. If possible, calm down before driving or pull over safely if you feel too emotional to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it always required to use your turn signals?
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
note: You must use your turn signal any time you intend to move left or right in a way that could affect other traffic. This includes changing lanes, turning at intersections, entering or leaving a parking space, and pulling into traffic from a curb, driveway, or alley. Signaling early and clearly lets other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians anticipate your movement and helps prevent collisions.

question: Which statements about driving on wet pavement are important to remember?
options: a:Wet pavement becomes especially slippery right after rain starts and can cause hydroplaning, so give yourself extra stopping distance.,b:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.,c:Wet roads do not affect cars with good tires.
note: When it first starts to rain, oil and debris on the road mix with water and make the surface very slick. Wet pavement also increases stopping distance and can cause hydroplaning, where your tires ride on top of the water and lose contact with the road. Slow down, avoid sudden moves, and leave extra space so you have more time to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, which driver has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who has the largest vehicle,b:The driver who arrived last,c:The driver who arrived first
note: At a four-way stop, the vehicle that comes to a complete stop first has the right-of-way and should go first. If two or more vehicles stop at the same time, the driver on the right goes first. If drivers are directly across from each other and one is turning left, the driver going straight has the right-of-way.

question: For persons 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of at least:
options: a:0.02 percent.,b:0.05 percent.,c:0.08 percent.,d:0.10 percent.
note: For drivers 21 and older in most U.S. states, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08% or higher. Even at lower levels, alcohol can impair judgment, reaction time, and coordination, so the safest choice is not to drive after drinking at all.

question: When you approach a steady red traffic light, you should:
options: a:Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.,b:Stop and remain stopped until the light changes to green or a right-on-red is legal and safe.,c:Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
note: A steady red light requires a full stop; you may turn right on red only if not prohibited and after yielding to pedestrians and traffic.

question: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:
options: a:Stop immediately in your lane regardless of conditions.,b:Drive alongside the vehicle and pass slowly.,c:Continue at the same speed if you are far enough away.,d:Move over a lane if possible, or slow down significantly and pass at a safe speed if you cannot change lanes.
note: If possible change lanes to give extra space; if not, slow down to a safe speed below the posted limit and give as much room as you can.

question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause a crash.
options: a:Take your attention away from the task of driving,b:Take your eyes off the road,c:Take your hands off the wheel,d:All of the above
note: Anything that takes your attention, eyes, or hands away from driving increases your crash risk. Mental distractions (attention), visual distractions (eyes off the road), and manual distractions (hands off the wheel) all reduce your ability to react quickly and control the vehicle, so all of these can lead to a collision.

question: Regulatory signs primarily:
options: a:Indicate actions a driver must or must not take.,b:Are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.,c:Are placed only where there is immediate danger.,d:Provide tourist information.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do under the law, such as speed limits, stop and yield signs, and no-turn signs. Obeying these signs is mandatory because they communicate legal requirements, not just suggestions or warnings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach a steady yellow traffic signal, what is the correct action?
options: a:Accelerate to get through before it turns red.,b:Stop unless you are already in the intersection.,c:Maintain speed because you have the right-of-way.,d:Turn on your hazard lights.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely or are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through carefully rather than braking hard in the middle of the intersection.

question: Why is it important to be alert to motorcycles?
options: a:They are smaller and more difficult to see, making speed and distance harder to judge.,b:They do not have the same rights as other vehicles.,c:They always signal when changing lanes.,d:They must ride on sidewalks.
note: Motorcycles are much smaller than cars and can be easily hidden in blind spots or by other vehicles. Because of their size, it is harder to judge how fast they are approaching and how far away they are. Drivers must look carefully for motorcycles, especially when changing lanes or turning.

question: As alcohol concentration in the blood increases, what happens?
options: a:Reactions slow down.,b:It begins to metabolize itself more quickly.,c:You become more alert.
note: As blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases, your reaction time slows, your judgment and coordination are impaired, and you may feel more confident than you should. This combination makes driving extremely dangerous even at relatively low BAC levels.

question: What is the safest practice for children riding in a vehicle?
options: a:They may be safely held by a strong adult.,b:They will be safe standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.,c:Children must be properly restrained in appropriate seats or safety belts.
note: Children must always be properly restrained in a child safety seat, booster seat, or seat belt appropriate for their age, size, and weight. Holding a child or letting them stand in the vehicle is extremely dangerous because they can be thrown forward or out of the vehicle in a crash or sudden stop.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do?
options: a:Turn off the engine and set the parking brake.,b:Stop the engine, remove the key, and lock the ignition.,c:Leave the engine running if you will be gone briefly.
note: When leaving a vehicle, stop the engine, remove the key, lock the ignition, and set the parking brake to prevent theft or unintended movement.

question: Which of the following about winter driving is not true?
options: a:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,b:Checking your vehicle's antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels is especially important during the winter.,c:Using cruise control in winter weather is a safe thing to do.
note: Winter driving is especially hazardous because of snow, ice, reduced visibility, and longer stopping distances, so your vehicle’s antifreeze and washer fluid must be in good condition. You should never use cruise control on snow, ice, or other slippery surfaces because you need full control of your speed and quick response to changing traction.

question: How should you safely pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.,b:Honk at the bicyclist to let them know you're passing.,c:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much room as possible.
note: Slow down and give bicyclists as much space as you safely can, ideally at least several feet. Do not drive in the bike lane or crowd them, and avoid honking in a way that could startle them.

question: How does increasing speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It has no effect on vision,b:It increases your field of vision,c:It only affects night vision,d:It decreases your field of vision, reducing ability to see hazards.
note: As your speed increases, your peripheral (side) vision effectively narrows and you see less of what is happening to the sides. This reduced field of vision makes it harder to detect hazards, so you must scan more carefully and avoid unnecessary speeding.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator sticks while driving, you should:
options: a:Continue driving to the next exit at speed.,b:Immediately turn the steering wheel sharply.,c:Open all windows and jump out.,d:Turn on hazard lights, shift to neutral, apply brakes, and steer off the road safely; then turn off the ignition.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep calm, turn on your hazard lights, shift to neutral so the engine is no longer driving the wheels, and use the brakes to slow down while steering to a safe place off the road. Once stopped, turn off the ignition without locking the steering wheel.

question: Which driving habit can help conserve gasoline?
options: a:Sitting with the engine idling in the driveway.,b:Accelerating quickly from every stop,c:Continuously shifting between lanes to find speed,d:Slowing down gradually and avoiding unnecessary stops.
note: Looking ahead and slowing down gradually instead of making sudden stops helps you maintain a steady speed, which uses less fuel. Hard acceleration, frequent lane changes, and idling waste gasoline.

question: A red arrow displayed on a traffic signal means:
options: a:A driver must stop for the movement indicated by the arrow and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears, unless a turn on red is permitted and not prohibited by signs.,b:A driver must proceed slowly through the intersection.,c:A driver must stop and then proceed straight when the way is clear.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped for the movement indicated by the arrow. In many states, you may turn right on a red right arrow (or left on a red left arrow from a one‑way to a one‑way) after stopping and yielding, unless a sign prohibits it. You may not proceed straight or make the indicated turn while the red arrow is displayed unless such a turn on red is specifically allowed by law and no sign forbids it.

question: If your vehicle’s right wheels leave the pavement, what is the correct action?
options: a:Open your door and inspect the right wheels,b:Slow gradually, steer parallel to the road, then gently steer back on when safe.,c:Stop immediately and turn sharply back onto the road.,d:Accelerate and yank the wheel to return to pavement quickly.
note: If your right wheels drop off the pavement, keep calm and avoid any sudden steering or braking. Ease off the accelerator, keep the steering wheel straight, and slow down gradually while your right wheels are on the shoulder. When the car is under control and traffic is clear, gently steer back onto the pavement at a shallow angle. Jerking the wheel or braking hard can cause you to lose control or skid into traffic.

question: If stopped at a railroad crossing that has multiple tracks, you should:
options: a:Proceed as soon as one train passes.,b:Start across immediately once the nearest train clears.,c:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before crossing.,d:Drive onto the tracks and wait for the next train.
note: At a crossing with multiple tracks, one train passing does not mean it is safe to go. Another train may be coming on a different track, sometimes hidden by the first train. Stay stopped until you can clearly see down all tracks in both directions and are sure no other trains are approaching, then cross only when it is completely safe and you can clear the tracks without stopping.

question: A lack of sleep affects driving similarly to which of the following?
options: a:The effect of alcohol.,b:The effect of amphetamines.,c:The effect of anger.
note: Drowsy driving slows your reaction time, harms judgment, and reduces awareness in a way very similar to alcohol impairment. Studies show that being awake for long periods, such as 18–24 hours, can affect driving ability about as much as having a moderate blood alcohol concentration. Because of this, you should never rely on willpower to stay awake; instead, rest before driving and take breaks on long trips.

question: Drivers may not pass from either side of which centerline configuration?
options: a:Double solid yellow centerline,b:Single broken yellow centerline,c:Combination solid and broken yellow line,d:Dashed white line
note: A double solid yellow centerline means vehicles in both directions are prohibited from passing. You must stay in your lane and may not cross the lines to overtake another vehicle. The only common exceptions are making a permitted left turn into or from a driveway or side road, or when directed by law enforcement. A single broken yellow line allows passing when safe, and a combination solid/broken line allows passing only for traffic on the broken-line side.

question: What typically causes hydroplaning?
options: a:Worn windshield wipers,b:Driving too fast on a wet road so tires cannot clear water.,c:Excessive acceleration on dry roads.,d:Frequent sudden stops.
note: Hydroplaning happens when you drive fast on a wet surface and your tires cannot push the water away quickly enough. A thin layer of water builds up between the tires and the road, causing the tires to lose contact and greatly reducing steering and braking control. To reduce the risk, slow down in rain, avoid standing water, and keep your tires properly inflated with good tread.

question: Why should you avoid following other cars too closely?
options: a:You will not see their turn signals.,b:It saves fuel to follow closely.,c:You may not see the road in front of you.,d:You may not have enough time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.
note: Following too closely, or tailgating, greatly reduces the time and space you have to react if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly. Keeping a safe following distance gives you enough room to brake smoothly and avoid rear-end collisions.

question: What lights should you use while driving in rain?
options: a:Low beam headlights,b:High beams,c:Parking lights only,d:Hazard lights while moving
note: In rain, you should use low beam headlights so you can see and be seen without glare. High beams reflect off rain, fog, or snow and can actually make it harder to see. Parking lights or hazard lights alone are not for driving and do not provide adequate visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing another vehicle is prohibited in which locations?
options: a:On hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings.,b:Only on one-way streets.,c:Anywhere there is a broken white line.,d:When the vehicle ahead is signaling a turn.
note: Passing is prohibited at places where you cannot clearly see oncoming traffic or where conflicts are likely, such as hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings. These areas often have no-passing markings because your view is limited and other vehicles may enter from side roads or tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From a center two-way left-turn lane you may:
options: a:Make U-turns only.,b:Make left turns only.,c:Make left turns and U-turns where permitted.
note: A center two-way left-turn lane is used only for making left turns from either direction, and for U-turns where they are specifically allowed. It is not a travel lane and must not be used for passing or for driving long distances.

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Lanes move in the same direction and drivers may pass or change lanes when safe.,b:Drivers may not pass,c:Indicates opposing traffic,d:Reserved bicycle lane
note: A single dashed white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and ensuring you will not interfere with other traffic.

question: To check blind spots when changing lanes, you should:
options: a:Use only the outside mirror without turning your head.,b:Turn your head and glance over your shoulder, not rely only on mirrors.,c:Close your eyes briefly to test reflexes.,d:Use only the inside rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see with your mirrors alone. Before changing lanes, quickly turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to make sure no vehicle, motorcycle, bicycle, or person is in that blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do before proceeding?
options: a:Drive slowly to let approaching traffic move out of your way.,b:Sound your horn to warn approaching pedestrians and vehicles.,c:Stop and proceed only after yielding to all pedestrians and vehicles on the roadway.
note: When entering a street from a driveway, alley, or private road, you must stop before the sidewalk or curb line and yield to all pedestrians and traffic on the roadway. Proceed only when it is safe and no pedestrians or vehicles are close enough to be a hazard.

question: If the driver behind you wants to pass, you should:
options: a:Slow down to create space in front of your vehicle for the other driver to pass.,b:Speed up to prevent the pass.,c:Move off the road immediately.,d:Flash your headlights and maintain speed.
note: If another driver wants to pass you, help them do it safely. Slightly reduce your speed to create more space in front of you so the passing driver has a larger gap to move back into your lane without cutting too closely in front of you.

question: If the accelerator sticks while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure to the brakes.,b:Shift directly into park.,c:Reach down and try to pull the pedal up.
note: If your accelerator sticks, keep calm and maintain control. Shift the transmission to neutral so the engine is no longer driving the wheels, then apply steady, firm brake pressure. Steer to a safe place off the road and stop. Once stopped, turn off the engine and address the mechanical problem.

question: When is it allowable to cross a dashed (broken) white line?
options: a:At any time, regardless of traffic conditions.,b:Only during daylight hours.,c:When it is safe and will not interfere with other traffic to change lanes.
note: A broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a broken white line to change lanes or pass, but only when you have checked your mirrors and blind spots and it is safe to move without interfering with other traffic.

question: Why is keeping a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:It provides time to react to unexpected actions by others.,b:It reduces distractions from nearby vehicles.,c:It ensures traffic flows faster,d:It allows you to drive less cautiously
note: Keeping a space cushion around your vehicle is essential because it gives you extra time and distance to see hazards and react smoothly. If another driver brakes suddenly, changes lanes, or makes a mistake, that open space lets you slow, stop, or steer away without needing a panic maneuver.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Look for a way around any lowered gates.,b:Be ready to drive faster than the train.,c:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
note: A railroad crossing warning sign means you are approaching train tracks and must be ready to slow or stop. Look and listen for trains, obey flashing lights and gates, and never drive around lowered gates or try to beat a train. Trains are much faster and take far longer to stop than road vehicles.

question: If you are being tailgated, you should:
options: a:Move over to the right, if there is an open lane to your right.,b:If there is not an open lane to your right, wait until the way is clear ahead and reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to pass.,c:Never slow down abruptly.
note: When being tailgated, your goal is to create space and avoid sudden moves. If there is an open lane to your right, safely move right and let the tailgater pass. If you cannot change lanes, wait until the road ahead is clear and then gradually reduce your speed to encourage the driver behind to go around you. Never slow or brake abruptly, because that can cause a rear‑end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Signaling before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb:
options: a:Is necessary only during the maneuver, not before.,b:Is a good driving habit and is required by law.,c:Is necessary only if other traffic is present.
note: Signaling is both a legal requirement and a key safety habit. You must signal well in advance—typically at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes in most areas, and often 200 feet or more at higher speeds—so others have time to see your signal and adjust. Always signal before you start the maneuver, even if you think no one else is around.

question: If you hear a siren but cannot immediately see the emergency vehicle, you should:
options: a:Keep driving until you spot it.,b:Pull to the curb, stop, and check whether it is on your street.,c:Slow down and continue driving.,d:Speed up to clear the way.
note: If you hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle, you must still yield the right‑of‑way. Safely pull as far to the right as possible and stop until you can locate the vehicle and are sure it is not approaching your path. This prevents you from accidentally blocking or cutting off an emergency responder.

question: What helps ensure safety while backing your vehicle?
options: a:Walk behind the vehicle to check for children and obstacles before getting in.,b:Check only your rearview mirror after entering the driver seat.,c:Honk before shifting into reverse,d:Look through a side window only
note: Before backing, walk behind your vehicle to check for children, pets, and objects that may be in your blind spots. Mirrors and cameras do not show everything, so physically checking the area helps prevent backing collisions.

question: When driving through an area where children are playing, you should expect that they may:
options: a:Wait at the curb before crossing.,b:Run out into the street without looking.,c:Always use a crosswalk.,d:Obey crossing guards without exception.
note: When driving where children are playing, expect that they may suddenly run into the street without looking. Children often misjudge speed and distance, so you must slow down, cover the brake, and be prepared to stop quickly.

question: How can you reduce your risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Use tires with proper air pressure.,b:Replace tires with bad tread.,c:Do not speed when the roads are wet.,d:All of the above
note: Hydroplaning is more likely with worn tires, low tread, improper air pressure, and higher speeds on wet roads. Keeping tires properly inflated, replacing worn tires, and slowing down on wet pavement all reduce the risk of losing traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Waiting to turn left when opposing traffic blocks your view, you should:
options: a:Wait until you can see all lanes to be crossed before completing the turn.,b:Wait for oncoming drivers to wave you through.,c:Begin turning as soon as the nearest lane is clear.,d:Edge into the intersection and stop there.
note: When turning left, do not start your turn until you can clearly see that all lanes you must cross are free of oncoming traffic. If your view is blocked, wait until you have a clear view rather than relying on other drivers or guessing.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around or under a railroad gate that is moving?
options: a:Only if no train is nearby.,b:If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.,c:No — do not go around or under a gate that is being lowered or raised.
note: Never drive around or under a railroad gate that is being lowered or raised, even if you do not see a train. Flashing lights and gates mean a train may be approaching, and you must stop and wait until the gates are fully raised and the signals stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light turns from green to yellow as you approach, your best action is to:
options: a:Speed up to beat the red.,b:Be prepared to stop if it is safe to do so.,c:Stop abruptly in the intersection.,d:Honk to warn other drivers.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should not speed up to beat the light. Instead, be prepared to stop if you can do so safely before entering the intersection. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through with caution.

question: When parking uphill on an incline with a curb, which way should you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Toward the curb (turn in),b:Turn slightly to the right regardless,c:Keep the wheels straight ahead,d:Sharp away from the curb (turn wheel away)
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels sharply away from the curb. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will touch the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic. Always set the parking brake as well.

question: Many crashes are caused by:
options: a:Driving too fast for conditions.,b:Checking mirrors frequently.,c:Yielding the right-of-way.,d:Driving at legal speeds.
note: Driving too fast for conditions is a major cause of crashes. Even if you are at or below the posted speed limit, you must slow down when roads are wet, icy, congested, or visibility is reduced. Safe speed is based on conditions, not just the number on the sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.,b:Only when driving in rural areas.,c:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.,d:When your slow speed unreasonably impedes traffic, except when reduced speed is necessary for safety.
note: Driving so slowly that you block or interfere with the normal, safe flow of traffic can be illegal. Minimum speed laws and “impeding traffic” rules require you to keep up with the reasonable flow of traffic (within the speed limit) when conditions allow. If you must drive much slower, you should move to the right lane or safely pull off the road.

question: Compared with daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:Less dangerous.,b:No more or less dangerous.,c:More dangerous.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous because you can see less far ahead, it is harder to judge speed and distance, and glare from headlights can reduce visibility. There is also a higher chance of encountering impaired or drowsy drivers. Use extra caution and reduce speed at night.

question: What color are regulatory signs usually, and must they be obeyed?
options: a:Blue and optional to follow,b:Green and advisory only,c:Yellow and warn about hazards,d:White background with black markings; they must always be obeyed.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do, such as speed limits, lane use, and parking rules. In the U.S., these are most commonly white with black letters or symbols, and they are legally enforceable, so you must obey them.

question: Which of the following can impair your ability to drive and lead to a DUII?
options: a:Inhalants such as glue or paint,b:Beer, wine, and other liquor,c:Controlled substances such as illegal drugs or some prescription medicines,d:All of the above
note: Any substance that affects your mind or body can impair driving, including alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many prescription or over‑the‑counter medicines. If it impairs your ability to drive safely, you can be charged with DUII regardless of whether the substance is legal.

question: Which safety restraints are most effective in a crash?
options: a:Only an airbag.,b:Only a lap belt.,c:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag used together.,d:No restraint if you have airbags.
note: The safest protection in a crash is using both the lap/shoulder belt and the airbag together. Seat belts keep you properly positioned so the airbag can work correctly and prevent you from being thrown forward or out of the vehicle.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke while driving affect your driving?
options: a:Has no effect on driving.,b:Is a distracting activity that can take your hands or eyes off the road.,c:Improves alertness.,d:Is required for long trips to stay awake.
note: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is a distraction. Reaching for cigarettes, lighting them, or dealing with dropped ashes can take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road, increasing your risk of a crash.
