question: How should drivers treat railroad crossings at all times?
options: a:As designated places to park temporarily.,b:As potentially dangerous; look and listen for trains before crossing.,c:As private property where no signals apply,d:As safe to cross because trains are rare.
note: Railroad crossings are always potential danger zones because trains are large, fast, and cannot stop quickly. You should slow down, look and listen for trains, and obey all warning signs, signals, and gates before crossing the tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're stopped in a line at a stop sign and the cars ahead clear the intersection with no cross traffic, what must you do?
options: a:Slowly roll past the stop sign so others know you are going,b:Honk and follow immediately,c:Proceed through without stopping since the way is clear.,d:Come to a complete stop again at the stop sign or line before proceeding.
note: At a stop sign, each driver must make their own complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. Even if the car ahead of you has already stopped and gone through, you must come to a full stop again before you proceed.

question: When driving on icy or snowy roads, which technique helps avoid crashes?
options: a:Add extra weight to your vehicle to improve traction.,b:Engage the four-wheel drive on your vehicle.,c:Reduce speed and increase following distance.
note: On icy or snowy roads, the most important safety steps are to slow down and leave much more space between you and the vehicle ahead. Lower speed reduces the chance of skidding, and extra following distance gives you more room to brake gently and avoid sudden steering or stopping, which can cause loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, you should:
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn on the shoulder.,b:Back up on the freeway to your exit.,c:Signal drivers to let you cut across.,d:Proceed to the next exit and safely turn around.
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway or interstate, you must never stop, back up, or make a U-turn on the roadway or shoulder. Continue to the next exit, leave the freeway safely, and then find a route that takes you back to your intended exit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout you must slow down and yield to which of the following?
options: a:No one.,b:Only motor vehicles.,c:Vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians already in or entering the roundabout.
note: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to all traffic already in the circle, as well as to pedestrians and bicyclists in crosswalks. Vehicles inside the roundabout have the right-of-way, so wait for a safe gap before entering.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal means that a ____ light will soon appear.
options: a:Flashing yellow.,b:Flashing red.,c:Steady green.,d:Steady red.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should stop if you can do so safely before the intersection; if you are too close to stop safely, proceed with caution before the light turns red.

question: If your tire suddenly blows out while driving, you should:
options: a:Slam on your brakes.,b:Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.,c:Keep driving normally.
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, stay off the brakes at first, and gently ease off the accelerator to maintain control. Once the vehicle has slowed and is stable, steer smoothly to the side of the road and brake lightly to come to a safe stop.

question: What does a steady green traffic light allow you to do?
options: a:Always turn without yielding to pedestrians,b:Stop and wait for it to change before moving.,c:Reverse through the intersection,d:Proceed through the intersection if the road is clear and turn when safe.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn if it is safe and not prohibited by signs, but you must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to oncoming traffic when turning left. Green never gives you the right to ignore other road users.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow in a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:The arrow is not used in traffic signals,b:You may turn without yielding,c:The turn is always protected,d:Prepare to stop and that the protected turn is ending (same as circular yellow)
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turning phase is ending. You should slow down and prepare to stop; the signal will soon change to a red arrow or another indication, and you will no longer have a protected turn.

question: Which practice helps prevent crashes by making your intentions known to other road users?
options: a:Tailgate to assert your position,b:Communicate using signals, horn, and predictable maneuvers.,c:Drive on side streets exclusively,d:Ignore other drivers and focus only on your driving.
note: Crashes are less likely when other road users can predict what you will do. Use turn signals, brake lights, your horn when needed, and make smooth, predictable maneuvers so others have time to react safely.

question: An inattentive driver is one who:
options: a:Only watches the vehicle ahead of their vehicle.,b:Stares at objects off the roadway or daydreams while driving.,c:Maintains eye contact during a conversation with a passenger while driving.
note: An inattentive driver is mentally or visually distracted from the driving task, such as daydreaming or staring at things off the roadway. Safe drivers keep their attention on the road, traffic, and driving environment at all times.

question: What is the most effective action to reduce your chance of injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Limit driving to weekdays.,b:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.,c:Wear your seat belt.
note: Wearing a seat belt is the single most effective way to reduce your risk of serious injury or death in a crash. Seat belts keep you from being thrown from the vehicle, spread crash forces over stronger parts of your body, and help you stay in position to maintain control.

question: Which factors influence alcohol's effects on you?
options: a:How much you drink, your body weight, and the time between drinks.,b:Only your tolerance to alcohol.,c:Only the type of alcohol consumed.,d:The color of the beverage.
note: Your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) and how alcohol affects you depend mainly on how much you drink, your body weight, and how quickly you drink over time. Drinking the same amount faster raises BAC more. Tolerance, drink color, or type of alcohol do not prevent impairment when the total alcohol amount is the same.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which factor greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:High speeds.,b:Night driving.,c:Driving slowly.,d:Wearing a seat belt.
note: As speed increases, your vehicle needs a much longer distance to stop, and the force of impact in a crash rises dramatically. Even small increases in speed greatly increase both stopping distance and crash severity, which is why obeying speed limits and slowing for conditions is critical.

question: When driving in fog, you should use your:
options: a:Parking lights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back at you, making it harder to see. Low beams, and fog lights if your vehicle has them, reduce glare and help you see the road and other vehicles more clearly.

question: When a parent/guardian signs a learner license consent form for a teenage applicant, they are indicating:
options: a:Their child has passed a driver education course.,b:Their child is a careful driver.,c:They accept financial responsibility for damage caused by the minor operating a motor vehicle.
note: When a parent or guardian signs a learner license or permit application for a minor, they are accepting financial responsibility for damages the minor may cause while driving. This means they can be held liable for costs resulting from crashes or violations committed by the minor.

question: You should increase following distance when you are:
options: a:Exiting an expressway.,b:Driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision.,c:Following a motorcycle.
note: You should increase your following distance whenever conditions make it harder to see or stop in time. This includes driving behind large vehicles that block your view, following motorcycles (which can stop more quickly and are harder to see), driving in bad weather, heavy traffic, or when someone is tailgating you. Leaving more space gives you more time to react and reduces the chance of a rear‑end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to change from the right lane to the left lane on a multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.,b:Look in your rearview mirror for traffic behind you before changing lanes.,c:Look in your side mirror for traffic and turn on your directional signal.
note: Before changing lanes, you should check your mirrors, signal, and then quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot. The over‑the‑shoulder check is what confirms that no vehicle is hidden where your mirrors cannot see. Only after you are sure the lane is clear should you smoothly change lanes.

question: What should your first response be to reduced visibility while driving?
options: a:Turn on hazard lights and stop in the lane,b:Turn on your windshield wipers only.,c:Turn on your interior light.,d:Reduce your speed.
note: When visibility is reduced, your first response should be to slow down. Reducing speed increases your time to see hazards and react safely. You should also use your headlights and windshield wipers as needed, but immediately lowering your speed is the most important first step to stay safe.

question: If you notice a defect on your vehicle that affects safety, you should:
options: a:Only fix it if you are stopped by police.,b:Correct the defect as soon as possible and not drive it if unsafe.,c:Ignore it until the next inspection.,d:Drive more slowly to compensate.
note: If your vehicle has a defect that could affect safety—such as bad brakes, worn tires, or broken lights—you should repair it as soon as possible and avoid driving the vehicle if it is unsafe. Driving with known safety defects increases your risk of a crash and can also be a violation of the law.

question: Which statement about work zones is correct?
options: a:Work zones use black-and-white regulatory signs only.,b:Work zones do not require reduced speed or extra attention,c:Work zones are only present at night,d:Work zones may be moving or stationary and are identified by orange signs.
note: Work zones can be either stationary (such as road repairs in one spot) or moving (such as line painting or mowing). They are identified by orange warning and regulatory signs. In and near work zones, you must slow down, follow posted instructions, and pay extra attention to workers, equipment, and changing traffic patterns.

question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Speed up to cross quickly,b:Stop and wait for a green signal.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.,d:Yield only to pedestrians
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield to pedestrians and other traffic if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, which actions are required?
options: a:Signal, check rearview and outside mirrors, and check blind spots by glancing over your shoulder.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Sound your horn before moving.
note: Before changing lanes, signal to let others know your intention, check your rearview and side mirrors, and then quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This ensures there is no vehicle in the area your mirrors cannot see.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Rapidly turn the steering wheel to maintain control,b:Honk repeatedly and keep driving at the same speed.,c:Turn off the engine immediately and stop in the lane.,d:Work harder to steer, reduce speed, and safely pull off the road.
note: If power steering fails, the vehicle will still steer but it will take much more effort. Keep a firm grip on the wheel, reduce your speed, signal, and carefully steer to the side of the road and stop in a safe place.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what should you not rely on exclusively?
options: a:Mirrors alone; you must also check blind spots by glancing over your shoulder.,b:Turn signals,c:Side clearance,d:Your speedometer
note: When changing lanes, you must not rely only on your mirrors because they leave blind spots. Always turn your head briefly to look over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change to be sure no vehicle is in your blind spot.

question: If you experience a tire blowout, you should:
options: a:Gradually slow down, avoid braking hard immediately, and steer to a safe location.,b:Immediately use full brakes.,c:Accelerate to stabilize the vehicle.,d:Turn off the engine and coast in traffic.
note: In a tire blowout, hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and avoid hard braking. Let the vehicle slow down gradually, then gently steer to the side of the road and stop in a safe place.

question: You notice the car ahead is distracted and driving with one hand talking to a passenger. What should you do?
options: a:Give the vehicle extra space.,b:Speed up to pass quickly.,c:Flash your lights to get their attention
note: When you see a driver who appears distracted, increase your following distance. Extra space gives you more time to react if they brake suddenly, drift in their lane, or make an unexpected move. Avoid speeding up or trying to get their attention, as that can create additional risk.

question: If you drink socially, which strategy best ensures you won't drive impaired?
options: a:Take a cold shower to reduce impairment,b:Arrange a ride home with someone who has not been drinking.,c:Drink coffee before driving to sober up,d:Drive slowly and hope for the best
note: The only reliable way to avoid driving impaired after drinking is to not drive at all. Arranging a ride with a sober driver, using a taxi, or using a rideshare ensures you are not behind the wheel while your blood alcohol content is still elevated. Coffee, cold showers, or driving slowly do not make you sober or safe to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection of two similar roads without signs or signals, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
options: a:The car approaching from the left has the right-of-way.,b:The car approaching from the right has the right-of-way.,c:The car in which the driver sounds his horn first has the right-of-way.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at about the same time, each driver must yield to the vehicle on their right. This rule helps prevent confusion when there are no signs or signals. If you see a vehicle approaching from your right, you should let that vehicle go first when it is safe.

question: Taking drugs together with alcohol:
options: a:Is less dangerous than alcohol alone.,b:Reduces the effect of alcohol on driving ability.,c:Increases the risk of causing a crash.
note: Alcohol and many drugs both affect judgment, coordination, and reaction time. When taken together, their effects can combine or multiply, making you far more impaired than with either substance alone. This greatly increases your chances of causing a crash, even if each substance is taken in what seems like a small amount.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, you must:
options: a:Maintain your normal driving speed.,b:Yield to pedestrians.,c:Stop and look for nearby police cars.
note: A green light allows you to turn right if it is not prohibited, but you must always yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any traffic that has the right-of-way. Slow down, check for pedestrians and oncoming vehicles, and complete the turn only when the path is clear.

question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:
options: a:Steady yellow light.,b:Flashing red light.,c:Yellow arrow.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look for other vehicles and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe. A steady yellow or yellow arrow is a warning that the light is about to change, not a mandatory stop if you can safely clear the intersection.

question: If a train is approaching and is a danger, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed across the tracks.,b:Not cross the tracks until the train has fully passed.,c:Cross the tracks at your own risk
note: If a train is close enough to be a danger, you must not cross the tracks. Wait until the train has completely passed, any crossing gates are fully raised, warning lights have stopped, and you can clearly see that the tracks in both directions are clear before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you should:
options: a:Ignore it and proceed at full speed.,b:Drive carefully through the intersection.,c:Stop and wait for it to change.,d:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. Slow down, be prepared to yield, and carefully scan for cross traffic, pedestrians, or hazards as you move through the intersection. You do not have to stop unless needed for safety or to yield the right-of-way.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is in your area, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to create distance.,b:Stop in place to block their path.,c:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely pull to the right side of the road and stop if possible, or otherwise make every safe effort to give it a clear path. Never speed up or block its route.

question: When are roads most slippery relative to rainfall?
options: a:When rain begins to freeze on the pavement.,b:Only after it has stopped raining.,c:After it has been raining continuously for several hours.,d:For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
note: Roads are often most slippery during the first 10–15 minutes of a rainstorm. Water mixes with oil and other residues on the road surface, creating a slick layer. As rain continues, much of this residue washes away and traction usually improves, though you should always drive carefully in wet conditions.

question: The best way to avoid alcohol-related crashes is to:
options: a:Simply say, No thanks, I'm driving, if someone offers you a drink.,b:Call a taxi.,c:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.
note: Deciding before you drink that you will not drive is the safest strategy. Once you start drinking, your judgment is impaired and you are more likely to underestimate how affected you are. Planning ahead—such as arranging a sober driver or alternate transportation—prevents you from being tempted to drive after drinking.

question: Brown-colored signs are used to indicate what type of area?
options: a:Construction zones,b:School zones,c:Regulatory restrictions,d:Public recreation or cultural/historical sites.
note: Brown traffic signs are used for guidance to public recreation areas and cultural or historic points of interest, such as parks, campgrounds, and historic sites. They are not used for construction, school zones, or regulatory rules.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:A school crossing zone.,b:A railroad crossing where drivers must yield to trains.,c:A pedestrian-only crossing.,d:A no-passing zone.
note: A crossbuck sign marks a railroad crossing. It functions like a yield sign: drivers must slow, look, and listen for trains and be prepared to stop. Trains always have the right-of-way, and you must never proceed if a train is approaching.

question: If you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle while on a divided multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Stop abruptly in your lane.,b:Continue at the same speed until near an exit.,c:Slow down, move to provide a clear path, and stop if necessary.,d:Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
note: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way by moving to create a clear path and stopping if needed. On a divided multilane highway, safely change lanes or move to the side and slow or stop so the emergency vehicle can pass quickly and safely.

question: When stopped in a line of traffic crossing railroad tracks without gates or signals, you must ensure:
options: a:You always stop before entering even if space is clear.,b:You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.,c:You may pass slower vehicles while crossing.,d:There is space ahead so your vehicle can clear all tracks without stopping.
note: Never enter a railroad crossing unless there is enough space on the far side for your entire vehicle to clear all the tracks without stopping. Being forced to stop on the tracks is extremely dangerous. You must wait behind the tracks until traffic ahead moves and you can cross completely in one continuous movement.

question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Turn off your brake lights to avoid alarming drivers behind.,b:Always slam on the brakes when approaching a stop.,c:Drive with no space ahead at high speeds.,d:Avoid sudden stops and allow your vehicle to slow before applying the brakes; use steady braking to stop smoothly.
note: To help prevent rear‑end collisions, slow your vehicle gradually. Ease off the accelerator first so the car begins to slow, then apply the brakes smoothly and steadily. This gives drivers behind you more time to see your brake lights and react, reducing the chance they will hit you from behind.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may legally pass another vehicle on the right when:
options: a:You are on a narrow bridge.,b:There is an available passing lane and the vehicle ahead is waiting to turn left.,c:It requires driving off the pavement.
note: You may pass on the right only when it can be done safely and without leaving the paved roadway. A common legal situation is when the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is a clearly marked lane or enough room in your lane to pass on the right while staying on the pavement. You must never pass on the right by driving off the road or on the shoulder.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, you should:
options: a:Accelerate quickly.,b:Do not proceed until the children wave to you.,c:Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
note: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, you must remain stopped until the stop arm is retracted and the red lights stop flashing. When you are allowed to proceed, move slowly and be prepared to stop again, watching carefully for children who may walk along the side of the road or cross unexpectedly.

question: When driving near large trucks, what must other road users allow for?
options: a:The increased stopping distance required by heavy vehicles.,b:The decreased stopping distance of large vehicles.,c:The quieter operation of large trucks,d:That trucks will always yield
note: Large trucks are heavy and need much more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. When driving near trucks, avoid cutting in front of them, don’t brake suddenly, and leave extra space so the truck driver has enough room and time to slow or stop safely.

question: When meeting an oncoming vehicle at night, what headlight setting should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights,b:Turn headlights off and use parking lights,c:Alternate between high and low beams,d:Low beam headlights
note: When an oncoming vehicle approaches at night, use low beam headlights. High beams can cause glare and temporarily blind other drivers. Low beams provide enough light for you to see while reducing glare so both drivers can maintain good visibility and control.

question: When executing a turn, what should you do with your speed?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Maintain your speed.,c:Reduce or adjust your speed to maintain control.
note: Reduce your speed before and during a turn so you can stay in your lane and keep full control of the vehicle. Entering a turn too fast makes it harder to steer, increases stopping distance, and raises the risk of skidding.

question: When you hear or see an emergency vehicle approaching, what should you do on a two-lane road?
options: a:Continue driving and allow them to maneuver around you.,b:Drive as far toward the right side of the road as is safe and stop.,c:Use the nearest driveway to let them pass
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights and siren, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as far to the right as is safe and stopping. Do not stop in an intersection; continue through if needed, then pull right and stop so the emergency vehicle has a clear path.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights of an approaching emergency vehicle, you must:
options: a:Slow down until it passes.,b:Drive to the right side of the road and stop.,c:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
note: You must yield to emergency vehicles using lights and siren by moving to the right side of the road and stopping. If you are in an intersection, clear the intersection first, then pull to the right and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.

question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:
options: a:A minor traffic safety problem.,b:A serious traffic safety problem.,c:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, reaction time, and coordination, so driving after drinking is a serious traffic safety problem. Even small amounts of alcohol can affect your ability to drive safely and greatly increase the risk of a crash.

question: What does an arrow painted in a traffic lane indicate?
options: a:Drivers in the proper lane must always come to a complete stop before making the movement only if required by a sign or signal.,b:Drivers in the proper lane may make the movement indicated by the arrow only when it is permitted by signs and signals.,c:Drivers must still obey traffic lights and signs that control the intersection, even when arrows are painted in the lane.,d:Drivers in the proper lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow.
note: Lane-use arrows painted on the pavement show which movement you must make from that lane, such as straight, left turn, or right turn. When you are in a lane marked with a single direction arrow, you are required to follow that direction, while still obeying any traffic signals or signs that control when you may proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in opposite directions, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Return when there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,b:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left shortly.,c:Return to the right side immediately after passing
note: On a two-lane road, you should only move back into your lane after passing when you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror and there is a safe space cushion. This ensures you do not cut too closely in front of the other driver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your direction, you should:
options: a:Always turn into the farthest lane from your approach.,b:Turn into any lane and then change immediately.,c:Turn into the middle lane regardless of your approach lane.,d:Turn into the lane closest to the lane you came from.
note: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your direction, you must turn into the lane closest to the one you came from. This keeps traffic organized and prevents side-swipe collisions with vehicles turning from other directions.

question: Two solid white lines painted across a lane denote a crosswalk. What must drivers do when pedestrians are in the crosswalk?
options: a:Drivers may proceed if no vehicle is coming.,b:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in the crosswalk.,c:Assume pedestrians must yield to vehicles
note: Two solid white lines across the lane mark a crosswalk. When pedestrians are in the crosswalk, drivers must yield the right-of-way and, if necessary, stop to allow them to cross safely before proceeding.

question: When meeting a school bus stopped with red lights flashing, drivers from either direction must:
options: a:Pass without stopping only if there is a physical median or barrier separating your direction of travel from the bus.,b:Stop at least the state-required minimum distance from the bus and do not proceed until the flashing red lights are off and the bus moves again.,c:Slow down and pass cautiously without stopping.,d:Proceed if no children are visible.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, drivers approaching from either direction must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the bus moves again. Many states require stopping at least 20 feet from the bus; some specify a greater distance. Always follow your state’s required minimum distance and never proceed while children may be entering or leaving the bus.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:Nothing significant occurs.,b:Alcohol cures common medication side effects.,c:The medicine always blocks alcohol's effects.,d:The combination can multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.
note: Combining alcohol with prescription or over-the-counter medicines can greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and impair judgment more than either substance alone. This makes driving much more dangerous, even if each substance alone might not seem very strong.

question: What effect can eating or drinking while driving have?
options: a:Drivers make no driving errors.,b:Drivers have trouble maintaining slow speeds.,c:It increases driver distraction and may reduce lane control
note: Eating or drinking while driving is a form of distraction. It can take one or both hands off the wheel and your eyes and attention off the road, which makes it harder to keep steady lane position and react quickly to hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed only.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Check mirrors and blind spots and signal your lane change.
note: Before changing lanes, always signal, check your mirrors, and quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This helps you see vehicles that may not appear in your mirrors and prevents cutting off another driver.

question: Which of the following is true about passing motorcycles?
options: a:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.,b:It is acceptable to pass a motorcycle within the same lane.,c:Drivers of other vehicles may follow motorcycles closely.,d:Motorcycles are entitled to the full width of a lane and must be passed by changing lanes entirely.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane just like any other vehicle. You should never try to share a lane with a motorcycle. When passing, move fully into the adjacent lane, pass safely with plenty of space, and then return only when it is clear.

question: Which feature is sometimes used on highways to channel drivers into the correct turning lanes?
options: a:Lane-use arrows and words painted on the pavement,b:Flashing yellow lights,c:Flashing red lights
note: Highways often use lane-use arrows and words painted directly on the pavement to guide drivers into the correct turning or through lanes in advance of an intersection. These pavement markings help drivers choose the proper lane early and reduce last‑second lane changes.

question: When changing lanes you should not:
options: a:Fail to check for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane.,b:Check your mirrors and signal.,c:Look over your shoulder to confirm the blind spot is clear.,d:Ensure there is enough space to complete the lane change.
note: When changing lanes, you must always check for other drivers, including those who may be moving into the same lane. Failing to check mirrors and blind spots can lead to sideswipe collisions, so you should never change lanes without thoroughly checking for nearby traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you signal while changing lanes or turning?
options: a:Always signal your intentions, even when no other traffic is visible.,b:Only if there is visible traffic present.,c:Only when driving at night
note: You must always signal before turning or changing lanes so that other road users can predict your movements. Even if you do not see other traffic, a pedestrian, cyclist, or unseen vehicle may be nearby, and signaling is required by law in all normal turning and lane-change situations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, what does this signal mean?
options: a:The driver is signaling for help.,b:The driver intends to turn right.,c:The driver intends to stop or slow.,d:The driver intends to turn left.
note: Hand signals are used when turn signals are not working or are hard to see. A left arm extended downward with the palm facing to the rear means the driver is slowing or stopping. Left arm straight out means a left turn, and left arm bent upward means a right turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when driving to an unfamiliar destination?
options: a:Plan your route in advance and consult a map or directions.,b:Rely solely on road signs to guide you,c:Drive with only a general idea of the destination,d:Stop frequently to ask random pedestrians
note: Planning your route before you drive reduces the need to look at maps, GPS, or signs at the last second. This helps you stay focused on the road, avoid sudden lane changes or turns, and drive more safely in unfamiliar areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp must:
options: a:Enter at any speed without checking traffic.,b:Expect drivers on the interstate to stop for them.,c:Yield to drivers already on the interstate and merge safely when possible.,d:Force their way into traffic.
note: Vehicles already on the interstate have the right-of-way. Use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge only when it is safe. Do not expect other drivers to stop or slow abruptly to let you in.

question: Which factor does stopping distance not depend on?
options: a:Your own reaction time.,b:The time of day.,c:The condition of your vehicle's brakes
note: Stopping distance is the sum of your reaction distance and braking distance. It is affected by your reaction time, speed, vehicle weight, and the condition of your brakes, tires, and the road surface. The time of day by itself does not change stopping distance, although visibility at night can affect how soon you notice hazards.

question: Which behavior is a common indicator that a driver may be intoxicated?
options: a:Weaving between lanes or making sudden stops.,b:Driving slightly below the speed of traffic only.,c:Using turn signals appropriately.,d:Keeping a constant lane position
note: Weaving across lanes, drifting, sudden stops, and other erratic movements are classic signs that a driver may be impaired. Alcohol and drugs affect judgment and coordination, so their driving often looks inconsistent and unpredictable compared with normal, steady driving.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do first?
options: a:Overcorrect the steering.,b:Turn your steering wheel into oncoming traffic.,c:Ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the vehicle to go.
note: When your vehicle begins to skid, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. This is often described as steering in the direction of the skid. Avoid slamming on the brakes or jerking the wheel, because sudden inputs can make the skid worse and cause you to lose control.

question: A red traffic signal light requires you to:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection.,b:Stop at the stop line only, even if it is past the crosswalk.,c:Proceed slowly if no traffic is present.
note: At a steady red light, you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection. If there is a stop line, stop at the line. If there is no stop line, stop before entering the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. The key requirement is that you are fully stopped before you move into the intersection area.

question: How is distracted driving best characterized?
options: a:Extremely risky behavior that increases the chance of a crash.,b:Very uncommon and of little concern.,c:Only a problem for new drivers.,d:Safe when done occasionally.
note: Distracted driving is any activity that takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving. It is extremely risky because even a brief distraction can cause you to miss hazards, drift from your lane, or fail to react in time to avoid a crash.

question: What may occur when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both may be increased.,b:Nothing will change.,c:All effects will be reduced.,d:You will sober up faster.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs often multiplies their effects. This can greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and impair judgment far more than either substance alone, making it much more dangerous to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look into the corresponding side mirror.,b:Look into the rearview mirror,c:Quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see with your mirrors alone. Before changing lanes, you must quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you intend to move to be sure no vehicle is hidden beside you.

question: A pennant-shaped traffic sign is used to indicate which situation?
options: a:School zones,b:Regulatory instructions,c:Speed limits,d:No passing zones
note: A pennant-shaped sign (a sideways triangle pointing to the right) is used specifically to mark the beginning of a no passing zone. It warns you not to start passing in that area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a busy freeway, how should you merge into traffic?
options: a:Use your mirrors and check blind spots, and adjust speed in the acceleration lane to match freeway traffic.,b:Yield to traffic only after stopping on the ramp.,c:Always stop at the end of the ramp before merging.
note: When entering a freeway, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches traffic, check your mirrors and blind spots, signal, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway before merging smoothly.

question: A bicyclist who disobeys traffic laws:
options: a:May be ticketed like a motor vehicle operator.,b:Is exempt from citations.,c:Will always be stopped and warned by police.,d:Cannot cause liability in an accident.
note: Bicyclists generally must follow the same traffic laws as drivers of motor vehicles. If they disobey traffic laws, they can be stopped and ticketed, and may be held liable in a crash.

question: \Highway hypnosis\" is caused by:"
options: a:Frequent rest stops.,b:Too much sleep the night before your trip.,c:Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
note: Highway hypnosis is a trance-like state that can occur when you stare straight ahead at the road for long periods without actively scanning. To prevent it, move your eyes regularly, take breaks, and stay mentally engaged.

question: Besides turn signals, what may communicate your intention to turn to other motorists?
options: a:Turning your wheels sharply in advance.,b:Braking hard several times,c:Flashing your headlights repeatedly.,d:Your vehicle position and eye contact.
note: Using your vehicle’s position in the lane and making eye contact with other road users can help communicate your intentions, but they must only supplement proper use of turn signals, not replace them. Avoid turning your wheels early, braking repeatedly, or flashing headlights as a way to signal a turn, because these actions can confuse or endanger other drivers.

question: If a flagger is controlling traffic in a construction zone, you must:
options: a:Assume the flagger is not supposed to be directing traffic.,b:Copy what surrounding traffic does regardless of the flagger's signals.,c:Follow the flagger's directions.
note: In construction and work zones, flaggers have the legal authority to direct traffic. You must follow their signals, even if they differ from traffic lights or signs. Obeying flaggers protects workers and drivers and is required by law in all states.

question: If your wheels slip off the edge of the pavement while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slam on the brakes and stop,b:Jerk the steering wheel sharply to return to the road immediately.,c:Speed up and bounce back onto the pavement quickly,d:Slow down gradually while driving with wheels off the pavement, then steer back when safe.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, keep calm, ease off the accelerator, and slow down gradually while keeping your wheels off the pavement. Once your speed is under control and it is safe, gently steer back onto the roadway. Jerking the wheel or braking hard can cause you to lose control or skid into traffic.

question: When you hear a siren behind you on the roadway, what must you do?
options: a:Pull over to the right and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.,b:Stop immediately where you are regardless of conditions.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.,d:Turn into the left lane and continue.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren, you must yield the right-of-way by safely pulling over to the right edge of the road and stopping until it has passed. Do not stop in the middle of a lane, speed up, or move left into its path, as this can block or delay the emergency response.

question: Drivers who have been drinking before driving generally:
options: a:Lack sufficient control over their bodies and judgment to drive safely.,b:Are always aware of the risks they are taking,c:Become better drivers because they are more careful,d:Are unaffected after a single drink
note: Alcohol reduces judgment, slows reaction time, and affects coordination, so drivers who have been drinking do not have the control needed to drive safely. Even one drink can impair driving ability, and people who are impaired often underestimate how affected they are.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you and a vehicle to your right arrive at the same time, you should:
options: a:Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.,b:Speed up and get through the intersection.,c:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you and another vehicle arrive at the same time, you must yield to the vehicle on your right. Slowing down and letting the vehicle on your right go first helps prevent confusion and collisions.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?
options: a:Never—mirrors are enough.,b:Only when parking.,c:Only when backing up.,d:When changing lanes, turning, or pulling toward or away from a curb.
note: Mirrors do not show everything around your vehicle; there are blind spots to the sides and slightly behind you. You should quickly look over your shoulder to check these blind spots when changing lanes, turning, or pulling toward or away from a curb to be sure the space is clear.

question: How should you negotiate turns on slick roads?
options: a:Change lanes quickly before the turn.,b:Accelerate quickly through the turn.,c:Take turns more slowly than usual
note: On slick or slippery roads, you have less traction, so it is easier to skid in a turn. Slow down more than usual before entering the turn and steer smoothly, avoiding sudden braking or acceleration while turning.

question: Driving while distracted by other activities generally:
options: a:Is never dangerous.,b:Usually causes the driver to react more slowly to hazards.,c:Usually causes the driver to drive faster.
note: Distractions such as using a phone, eating, or adjusting controls take your attention away from driving. This usually slows your reaction time and makes it harder to notice and respond to hazards in time to avoid a crash.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams, where should you look to reduce glare?
options: a:Toward the left side of the road.,b:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,c:Toward the right side of the road.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, avoid looking directly at the bright lights. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road to reduce glare while still using the road edge as a guide to stay in your lane.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing without gates or flashing lights, how should you act?
options: a:Cross quickly without looking,b:Change gears while on the tracks to prevent stalling,c:Always stop before crossing regardless of visibility.,d:Be prepared to yield to any train and ensure your entire vehicle can clear the tracks.
note: At an ungated railroad crossing, slow down, look and listen for trains in both directions, and only proceed when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough room for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks without stopping. Never stop or shift gears while on the tracks, because stalling or hesitating on the rails is extremely dangerous.

question: A traffic light showing a green arrow and a red light means you may:
options: a:Drive only if you proceed straight ahead.,b:Drive only in the direction of the green arrow.,c:Wait for a solid green light before moving in any direction.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected movement in the direction the arrow points, even if the main signal is red. You may go only in the direction of the green arrow, after yielding to any pedestrians or vehicles already in the intersection; you must stop for the red light for all other directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes, which of the following is important?
options: a:Signal your intentions ahead of the lane change.,b:Check your blind spot.,c:Make sure the lane is clear before entering.,d:All of the above.
note: Before changing lanes, you must signal in advance, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, then move only when the lane is clear. All of these steps work together to make sure other drivers know your intentions and that you are not moving into a space already occupied or about to be occupied by another vehicle.

question: On a highway divided by two solid yellow lines, when may you cross them?
options: a:Never under any circumstance,b:To overtake bicycles only,c:To pass another vehicle if no oncoming traffic is visible,d:Only to make a left turn into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.
note: Two solid yellow lines mean no passing in either direction. You may not cross them to pass another vehicle, but you may carefully cross them to make a left turn into or out of a driveway, alley, or private road when it is safe and not otherwise prohibited by signs.

question: If you are taking an over-the-counter medication, you should:
options: a:Read the labels on the drug before driving.,b:Continue to drive regardless of any warning labels.,c:Drink alcohol instead.
note: Many over-the-counter medicines can cause drowsiness, blurred vision, or slowed reaction time. Always read the label before driving and follow any warnings about operating a vehicle. If the label is unclear or you feel affected, ask a doctor or pharmacist and avoid driving until you know it is safe.

question: An “End school zone” sign means:
options: a:Children are present all day.,b:You must reduce speed to 20 mph.,c:The reduced school-zone speed limit has ended.,d:The school zone speed begins here.
note: An “End school zone” sign tells you that the special reduced speed limit for the school zone is over. After passing this sign, you may resume the regular posted speed for that roadway, as long as conditions are safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you pass another vehicle?
options: a:When your lane is next to a broken yellow line and the other lane is clear ahead.,b:In a curve or on a hill if you think there is little chance of oncoming traffic.,c:By using the shoulder of the highway.
note: You may pass another vehicle only when it is both legal and safe. A solid yellow line on your side of the center line means passing is not allowed. You must not pass on hills, curves, or anywhere your view of oncoming traffic is limited, and you may never pass by driving on the shoulder.

question: You may pass another vehicle if the line dividing your lane from the lane you wish to enter is a:
options: a:Broken yellow line on your side of the center.,b:Double solid yellow line.,c:Solid yellow line.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and may be crossed when changing lanes, not for passing into oncoming traffic. To pass a vehicle traveling in the opposite direction, you look for a broken yellow center line on your side of the road, which indicates that passing is allowed when it is safe.

question: At a light rail crossing, you should always:
options: a:Look both ways before crossing tracks and obey signals.,b:Drive around lowered gates if you can.,c:Assume trains will stop for vehicles.,d:Cross without stopping if no train is visible.
note: At a light rail or train crossing, always slow, look both ways, and be prepared to stop. Obey all warning signs, flashing lights, and gates. Never drive around lowered gates or assume a train will stop for you; trains need a long distance to come to a complete stop.

question: When are you allowed to cross double solid yellow center lines?
options: a:To pass a slow-moving vehicle at any time.,b:To pass another car when there is no oncoming traffic.,c:To change lanes quickly,d:To turn left into or out of a driveway or to make a permitted left turn.
note: Double solid yellow center lines mean no passing or lane changes in either direction. The main exception is when you are making a left turn into or out of a driveway, side road, or alley, or making another permitted left turn such as a legal U-turn where allowed.

question: A double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: A double solid yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed from either side. You may cross these lines only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe, but you must not use the opposing lane to pass other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an intersection and the light turns solid yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Stop before entering if you can do so safely; otherwise proceed through cautiously.,b:Speed up to beat the red.,c:Treat it as a green and go normally,d:Immediately stop in the middle of the intersection
note: A solid yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through the intersection with caution and do not speed up to beat the red.

question: Round traffic signs typically warn of:
options: a:School zones.,b:Upcoming railroad crossings.,c:No passing zones.
note: Round traffic signs are used specifically to warn of a railroad crossing ahead. When you see a round railroad warning sign, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: You must yield to an emergency vehicle when:
options: a:You see flashing lights or hear a siren.,b:Only if it is following traffic lawfully.,c:Never — emergency vehicles yield to you.,d:Only during daytime hours.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using a siren and/or flashing lights. Safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by a police officer.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, where should you stop?
options: a:Stop immediately where you are.,b:Stop on the right side of the roadway.,c:Stop and wait only until the light turns green.
note: When you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle using a siren or flashing lights, you should pull over to the right edge of the roadway and stop. Remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed and it is safe to reenter traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, you should:
options: a:Go to the next exit.,b:Make a U-turn through the median.,c:Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway, stay calm, keep going, and take the next exit. Never stop in a travel lane, back up on the freeway, or make a U-turn through the median, because these actions are illegal and extremely dangerous at high speeds.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign generally indicate?
options: a:An interstate route marker.,b:A school crossing only.,c:A regulatory prohibition.,d:Warning of road hazards or special conditions ahead.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are used for warnings. They alert you to road hazards, changes in road conditions, or special situations ahead so you can slow down and be prepared. They are usually yellow for general warnings and orange in work zones.

question: Which condition increases your vehicle's stopping distance?
options: a:When driving at night.,b:On a wet or icy road.,c:On paved highways.,d:When using cruise control.
note: Your stopping distance increases when traction is reduced, such as on wet, icy, snowy, or gravel roads. With less grip, your tires need more distance to slow and stop, so you must reduce speed and increase your following distance in these conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed through an intersection that has a stop sign but no marked stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:Only if you have to stop at least 20 feet away,b:After honking to alert others,c:After coming to a complete stop at a point where you can see traffic and it is safe to go.,d:After slowing slightly to check for traffic but not stopping.
note: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection at the point where you can best see approaching traffic. After stopping and yielding to any pedestrians and vehicles with the right-of-way, proceed only when it is safe.

question: If involved in an accident, a driver must:
options: a:Stop at or near the scene, move vehicles out of traffic if possible, and turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles.,b:Leave immediately and report later.,c:Refuse to provide any information.,d:Continue driving if damage is minor.
note: If you are involved in a crash, you must stop at or near the scene, help prevent further danger by moving vehicles out of traffic if it is safe to do so, and turn off the ignitions of wrecked vehicles to reduce fire risk. You must also exchange information and, when required, report the crash to police.

question: How can you reduce the chance of hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive faster to get through wet areas quickly.,b:Drive more slowly in wet conditions.,c:Follow closely behind the vehicle ahead.,d:Shift to neutral when water is deep.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road, usually at higher speeds. Slowing down in wet conditions helps your tires push water aside and maintain traction, greatly reducing the risk of hydroplaning.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by which color lines?
options: a:White,b:Black,c:Yellow,d:Red
note: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Knowing this color code helps you quickly understand how traffic is flowing and where passing may or may not be allowed.

question: To ensure your physical condition does not make driving unsafe, you should:
options: a:Keep physically fit and have regular physical examinations.,b:Know the effect of any medicine on your driving ability.,c:Drive within your physical limitations.,d:All of the above
note: Safe driving depends on your health and abilities. Staying physically fit, understanding how any medications affect you, and driving within your physical limits all help ensure you can react properly and stay in control of your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may drive left of a highway's centerline:
options: a:When overtaking and passing another vehicle, if passing is permitted and it is safe to do so.,b:When you have at least 200 feet of clear road ahead.,c:When the shoulder of the road is rough and the ditch is deep.
note: You may cross the centerline to pass another vehicle only where passing is allowed and it is safe—typically indicated by a broken yellow line on your side and enough clear space ahead. You must never cross solid yellow lines or pass where signs or road markings prohibit it, even if the road appears clear.

question: On slippery roads, what should you do to improve safety?
options: a:Drive as you would on dry roads.,b:Use alternate routes.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: On slippery roads, your tires have less grip and it takes longer to stop. Increasing your following distance gives you more time and space to brake gently and avoid skids or rear-end collisions.

question: Which practice can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Driving as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.,b:Constantly switching lanes to gain advantage.,c:Honking frequently to assert yourself.,d:Allowing extra travel time and using proper signals.
note: Allowing extra travel time, using turn signals, and obeying speed limits helps you stay calm and predictable. When you are not rushed and you communicate clearly, you are less likely to get frustrated or provoke other drivers, which reduces the chances of road rage or aggressive driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:
options: a:Accelerate into the turn to clear traffic.,b:Always stop in the middle of the intersection.,c:Turn from any lane regardless of markings.,d:Signal several seconds in advance, check mirrors, slow gradually, and watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
note: For a left turn, you should signal well in advance, check mirrors and blind spots, slow down smoothly, and watch carefully for oncoming traffic, pedestrians, and cyclists. You must yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians in the crosswalk before turning.

question: If you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, what is the first action you must take?
options: a:Determine if anyone is injured.,b:Call the police.,c:Stop your vehicle.
note: If you are involved in a crash, the law requires that you stop at once. Stopping your vehicle is the first step so you do not leave the scene and so you can secure the area. After stopping, if it is safe, move the vehicle out of traffic, check for injuries, call emergency services if needed, and exchange information and report the crash as required by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should you reduce speed when exiting a highway?
options: a:Once you have moved into the exit lane and are on the deceleration ramp.,b:On the main highway just before the exit lane.,c:Only after you see a toll booth,d:After you pass the exit sign
note: You should maintain highway speed until you are in the exit lane, then slow down on the deceleration ramp. Slowing on the main highway before entering the exit lane can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: The best ways to avoid hydroplaning include:
options: a:Keep your tires properly maintained.,b:Watch out for standing water or puddles.,c:Slow down when roads are wet.,d:All of the above
note: Hydroplaning is more likely with worn or underinflated tires, higher speeds, and standing water. Keeping tires in good condition, watching for puddles, and slowing down on wet roads all help your tires maintain contact with the pavement and reduce the risk of losing control.

question: Which is the leading cause of fatalities on Montana roads?
options: a:Poor or unkempt roads,b:Inclement weather/driving conditions,c:Drunk drivers
note: Alcohol‑impaired driving is consistently one of the leading causes of traffic deaths in Montana and across the U.S. Poor road conditions or bad weather can contribute to crashes, but impaired drivers cause far more fatal collisions. Because of this, avoiding drinking and driving is critical for safety.

question: How should you respond to a flashing red traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Stop only if other cars are approaching.,b:Come to a full stop and proceed when safe.,c:Slow down and proceed without stopping
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, yield the right‑of‑way as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe. You may not just slow down or stop only if other vehicles are present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do before making a left turn?
options: a:Sound your horn loudly,b:Swing to the right then back left,c:Speed up to clear the turn quickly,d:Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: Before making a left turn, you must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Turn only when there is a safe gap so you do not force oncoming drivers to brake or swerve. Swinging wide, speeding up, or using the horn are not proper or safe ways to make a left turn.

question: When merging onto a freeway, what is the best practice?
options: a:Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.,b:Use the on-ramp to accelerate to freeway speed and blend with traffic.,c:Turn on your hazard lights until fully merged
note: When using a freeway on‑ramp, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed close to that of freeway traffic, signal, and merge into a suitable gap. Entering too slowly can cause other drivers to brake or swerve, and hazard lights are not used for normal merging.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than:
options: a:The maximum speed limit at all times.,b:Any speed that keeps up with traffic flow.,c:Twice the posted speed limit.,d:A speed that is reasonable and prudent for conditions even if below the posted maximum.
note: You must never drive faster than is reasonable and prudent for current conditions, even if that is below the posted speed limit. In rain, snow, fog, heavy traffic, or poor visibility, you are required to slow down. The posted limit is a maximum under ideal conditions, not a target speed.

question: What does a solid white centerline on a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,c:Lanes moving in the same direction and drivers may pass when safe
note: A solid white line is used to separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and indicates that lane changes are discouraged or sometimes prohibited. A centerline between opposing directions of travel is normally yellow, not white. So a solid white centerline on a two-lane road indicates same-direction traffic with restricted lane changing, not opposite-direction traffic.

question: A flashing yellow traffic light means:
options: a:Merging traffic,b:Pedestrian crossing,c:Proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow traffic signal means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, yielding as necessary. It does not require a full stop, but you must be prepared to react to other traffic, pedestrians, or unexpected hazards.

question: If you move, you must report your address change to the Driver License Bureau within:
options: a:Two weeks.,b:10 days.,c:15 days.,d:One month.
note: Many states require you to report an address change within a short, specific time frame, often 10 days, so that your license and records stay current and important notices can reach you. Always check your own state’s exact requirement, but the key idea is that you must notify the licensing agency promptly after you move.

question: The effect alcohol has on reflexes and judgment is:
options: a:Most pronounced when consuming hard ciders and mixed drinks.,b:Less pronounced when consuming beer instead of wine.,c:Less pronounced when consuming wine instead of beer.,d:Dependent on how much alcohol is in the bloodstream, not the type of beverage.
note: Alcohol’s effect on your reflexes and judgment depends on how much alcohol is in your bloodstream (your BAC), not whether it came from beer, wine, or liquor. A standard serving of each has about the same amount of pure alcohol, so any type can impair you equally if it results in the same BAC.

question: To prepare for hazards ahead, you should:
options: a:Stare straight ahead at all times.,b:Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.,c:Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.
note: To spot hazards early, you should constantly scan the road ahead, to the sides, and check mirrors regularly. This wide scanning helps you see changing traffic, pedestrians, and road conditions in time to adjust your speed or position safely.

question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, you should:
options: a:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,b:Stay in the driver's blind spot.,c:Keep a steady pace.
note: Staying in another driver’s blind spot is dangerous because they may change lanes or turn without seeing you. Either gently speed up to move ahead where you are visible in their mirrors, or ease off the accelerator to fall back so you can see their face in the side mirror. That’s your cue that they can see you.

question: When approaching a flashing yellow light, you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop completely every time.,c:Turn on your headlights.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution, watching carefully for cross traffic, pedestrians, or other hazards. You are not required to stop unless needed for safety, but you must be prepared to yield if another road user has the right-of-way.

question: If you are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, you must:
options: a:Drive with your flashers turned on.,b:Speed up and take the nearest exit.,c:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches on a one‑way street, you must move safely and promptly toward the nearest edge or curb—right or left—and stop until it has passed. Stopping at the roadside gives the emergency vehicle a clear path and reduces the chance of a collision.

question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Keep your speed constant once in the exit ramp.,b:Slow down once you move onto the exit ramp.,c:Slow down after you have entered the exit ramp and are clear of freeway traffic.
note: On freeways, traffic is moving at high speed, so you should not slow down while still in the main travel lane to exit. Instead, signal and move into the exit lane at freeway speed, then reduce speed as needed after you are fully in the exit ramp and within any posted ramp speed limit. Slowing before entering the ramp can cause rear‑end collisions in the through lane.

question: When driving in traffic, what is generally the safest approach regarding speed?
options: a:Fluctuate your speed to stay alert.,b:Drive faster than the flow of traffic.,c:Maintain a speed consistent with the flow of traffic and posted limits
note: Driving much faster or much slower than surrounding traffic increases the risk of collisions because other drivers must brake, change lanes, or react suddenly. The safest approach is to travel at a speed that matches the general flow of traffic while staying within the posted speed limit and adjusting for conditions such as weather and visibility.

question: An advisory speed sign attached to a curve warning means you should:
options: a:Ignore the advisory in rainy or icy conditions.,b:Speed up when entering the curve.,c:Reduce speed in poor conditions rather than ignoring the advisory.,d:Always maintain the posted highway limit.
note: Advisory speed signs on curves show a recommended safe speed under ideal conditions, not a mandatory limit. In rain, snow, or ice, you should slow even more than the advisory speed so you can maintain control and traction through the curve.

question: When entering the roadway from a private road or driveway, what is required of you?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and vehicles already on the roadway.,b:Enter quickly without stopping if the road looks clear.,c:Sound your horn to warn approaching traffic,d:Stop with part of your vehicle on the roadway to alert others
note: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must yield to all pedestrians and vehicles already on the road. Enter only when it is safe, without forcing others to slow or change lanes for you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an uncontrolled intersection, you should:
options: a:Maintain your speed and proceed.,b:Stop at the intersection, check in all directions, and proceed.,c:Slow down, look in all directions, and yield to a vehicle approaching from the right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, you must slow down, look carefully in all directions, and be prepared to stop. If two vehicles arrive at about the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. You still adjust your speed and approach cautiously rather than just driving through at full speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is crossing a single broken white or yellow line not allowed?
options: a:When turning left into a driveway.,b:When doing so would interfere with traffic.,c:When the car in front of you is disabled.,d:When a solid line is next to your lane instead of a broken line.
note: A single broken line—white between lanes in the same direction or yellow between opposite directions—may be crossed to pass or change lanes only when it is safe. You must not cross if doing so would interfere with oncoming or adjacent traffic, such as forcing another driver to brake or swerve.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, what should you assume?
options: a:That the driver will open the car door or a passenger may step out as you approach.,b:That the driver will wait for you to pass.,c:That the parked vehicle will roll into the street.,d:That nothing around the parked vehicle will change.
note: When passing a vehicle that is parked or just pulled to the curb, you should expect that a door might open or a person might step out suddenly. Slow if needed and leave extra space so you can avoid a collision if someone opens a door into your path.

question: Which color lines separate lanes moving in the same direction?
options: a:White,b:Yellow,c:Red
note: White lane lines (solid or broken) are used to separate traffic moving in the same direction. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, and red is not used to separate lanes of travel.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings and other markings?
options: a:They are usually not important.,b:They are only used in construction zones.,c:They provide drivers with information
note: Pavement markings give important information about where you may drive, pass, stop, or turn. They help you stay in the correct lane, indicate turn lanes and crosswalks, and warn of changes or hazards ahead.

question: When parallel parking between two cars, you should first:
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left.,b:Turn your wheels to the right.,c:Pull up even with the car in front of your desired parking space.
note: For standard parallel parking, after signaling and checking traffic, you pull up alongside and even with the vehicle in front of the space. From there you begin backing into the space while turning the wheel as appropriate.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Either lane,b:The left lane (closest to the left curb),c:The right lane
note: When turning onto a one-way street, turn into the lane nearest to the direction you entered from, unless signs indicate otherwise.

question: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) depends on each of the following, except:
options: a:Your body weight.,b:How much you drink.,c:How much time passes between drinks.,d:The type or name of the alcoholic beverage you drink.
note: Your BAC is determined by how much alcohol you consume, your body weight, and how quickly you drink (time between drinks). The type or flavor of alcoholic beverage does not change how your body processes alcohol; what matters is the total amount of pure alcohol you take in.

question: Worn or bald tires can:
options: a:Increase stopping distance and make turning more difficult.,b:Reduce fuel consumption.,c:Improve traction in wet conditions.,d:Ensure a smoother ride.
note: Tires with worn or bald tread cannot grip the road well. This increases your stopping distance, makes steering and turning less precise, and greatly raises the risk of skidding or hydroplaning on wet roads. Keeping good tread depth is essential for safe braking and control.

question: How should you pass a bicyclist on a two-lane road that has no bicycle lanes?
options: a:Wait until no oncoming traffic, then pass leaving sufficient space.,b:Pass immediately and move back into lane quickly.,c:Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign
note: When passing a bicyclist, you must treat the bicycle like a slow-moving vehicle and only pass when it is safe. Wait for a clear gap in oncoming traffic, then move over and leave at least 3 feet of space (or more at higher speeds) before returning to your lane. Never squeeze past a bicyclist in the same lane when there is oncoming traffic.

question: What do pentagonal traffic signs indicate?
options: a:Speed limits,b:School zones,c:No passing zones
note: Pentagonal (five-sided) signs are used for school zones and school crossings. When you see this shape, slow down, watch carefully for children, and be prepared to stop for pedestrians in or near the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You plan to turn left but oncoming traffic is heavy. What is the correct course of action?
options: a:Use the next intersection or another safe location to turn if you cannot complete the left turn safely.,b:Wait behind the crosswalk or stop line until traffic clears enough to turn safely.,c:Enter the center of the intersection and wait for an opening even if you cannot complete the turn before the light changes.
note: On many modern exams, the safest and more universally legal guidance is to wait behind the crosswalk or stop line until you have a safe gap to turn left, or use the next intersection or a different route if traffic is too heavy. Some states allow entering the intersection on green to wait, but others require you to stay behind the stop line. Because rules differ, the safest general practice is not to pull into the intersection if you cannot complete the turn safely and legally.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what safety routine should you follow?
options: a:Be sure all passengers, including children, have buckled their seat belts.,b:Be sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.,c:Be sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts
note: Before starting the vehicle, make sure everyone is properly buckled, including children and back-seat passengers. The driver is responsible for ensuring that all occupants use seat belts or appropriate child restraints, which greatly reduces the risk of injury in a crash.

question: Your blind spot is the area:
options: a:You cannot see without moving your head (not visible in mirrors).,b:Directly behind your vehicle only.,c:You see in your rearview mirror.,d:Inside your vehicle cabin only.
note: Blind spots are the areas around your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors alone. To check them, you must briefly turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes or turning.

question: When a traffic signal shows a flashing yellow arrow for left turns, drivers:
options: a:Must come to a complete stop before turning.,b:Should merge into the lane indicated by the arrow without yielding.,c:Are prohibited from turning left.,d:May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow left-turn arrow means you may turn left, but only after yielding to oncoming traffic, bicyclists, and pedestrians. Oncoming traffic has the right-of-way, and you must wait for a safe gap before turning.

question: When preparing to change lanes, you should:
options: a:Signal and immediately move over.,b:Check mirrors, signal, and glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot.,c:Only check your side mirror.,d:Change lanes without signaling if traffic is light.
